knowledge_statements.statement_title: Bounded-Variation Characterization of Univariate DC Functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterization on [0,a], including finiteness of the indicated one-sided endpoint derivatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A function f:[0,a]\to\mathbb{R} admits a representation f=p-q with convex p,q:[0,a]\to\mathbb{R} and finite p'_+(0),p'_-(a),q'_+(0),q'_-(a) if and only if there exists a bounded-variation function r:[0,a]\to\mathbb{R} such that f(x)=f(0)+\int_0^x r(t)\,dt for every x\in[0,a].
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A univariate function on [0,a] has a DC decomposition whose convex components have finite indicated endpoint one-sided derivatives exactly when it is the integral of a bounded-variation function, up to its value at zero.
assumptions_latex: f:[0,a]\to\mathbb{R}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bigl[\exists\text{ convex }p,q:\ f=p-q,\ p'_+(0),p'_-(a),q'_+(0),q'_-(a)\in\mathbb{R}\bigr]\iff\bigl[\exists r\in BV([0,a]):\ \forall x\in[0,a],\ f(x)=f(0)+\int_0^x r(t)\,dt\bigr]

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition on a convex subset of Euclidean space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let S\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n be convex. A function f:S\to\mathbb{R} is difference-of-convex (DC) on S if there exist convex functions p,q:S\to\mathbb{R} such that f(x)=p(x)-q(x) for every x\in S.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A real-valued function on a convex set is DC if it is the difference of two convex functions on that set.
assumptions_latex: S\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\text{ is convex}
f:S\to\mathbb{R}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\text{ is DC on }S\iff \exists\text{ convex }p,q:S\to\mathbb{R}\;\forall x\in S,\ f(x)=p(x)-q(x)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Extracted Closed-Ball Definition of a Locally DC Function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The extract explicitly permits radius zero; this makes the condition degenerate unless a positive-radius requirement is imposed elsewhere.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For x_0\in\mathbb{R}^n and \epsilon\ge 0, let B(x_0,\epsilon)=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:\|x-x_0\|\le\epsilon\}. A function f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R} is locally DC in the extracted sense if, for every x_0\in\mathbb{R}^n, there exists \epsilon\ge 0 such that f|_{B(x_0,\epsilon)} is DC.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In the extracted definition, every point must have a closed ball on which the function is DC, but the permitted zero radius creates a degenerate boundary case.
assumptions_latex: f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}
B(x_0,\epsilon)=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:\|x-x_0\|\le\epsilon\}
\epsilon\ge 0
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\text{ is locally DC in the extracted sense}\iff \forall x_0\in\mathbb{R}^n\;\exists\epsilon\ge0:\ f|_{B(x_0,\epsilon)}\text{ is DC}

knowledge_statements.title: Basic Composite DC Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite maxima and minima of real-valued DC functions on a common convex domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be convex and let \(f_i=g_i-h_i\) on \(C\), where \(g_i,h_i:C\to\mathbb{R}\) are convex for \(i=1,\ldots,m\). With \(H=\sum_{j=1}^m h_j\), one has
\[
\max_{1\le i\le m}f_i=\max_{1\le i\le m}\left(g_i+\sum_{j\ne i}h_j\right)-H.
\]
The maximum on the right is convex, so the displayed formula is a DC representation. Moreover,
\[
\min_{1\le i\le m}f_i=-\max_{1\le i\le m}(-f_i),
\]
and therefore every finite minimum is also DC.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite maxima and minima of DC functions are DC, with an explicit decomposition obtained by collecting all convex negative components.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is convex.
\(m\in\mathbb{N}\) is finite.
\(g_i\) and \(h_i\) are finite convex functions on \(C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\max_i f_i\) and \(\min_i f_i\) admit explicit DC representations on \(C\).

notation.meaning: DC decomposition of the ith function

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite linear combinations of real-valued DC functions on a common convex domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be convex and \(f_i=g_i-h_i\), where \(g_i,h_i:C\to\mathbb{R}\) are convex. For \(a_i\in\mathbb{R}\), write \(a_i^+=\max\{a_i,0\}\) and \(a_i^-=\max\{-a_i,0\}\). Then
\[
\sum_{i=1}^m a_i f_i=
\left(\sum_i a_i^+g_i+\sum_i a_i^-h_i\right)-
\left(\sum_i a_i^+h_i+\sum_i a_i^-g_i\right),
\]
so every finite real linear combination is DC on \(C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite real linear combinations of DC functions are DC, with negative coefficients exchanging the two convex components.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is convex.
Each \(f_i\) has a finite convex-minus-convex representation on \(C\).
The family is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{i=1}^m a_i f_i\) is DC on \(C\).

notation.meaning: positive and negative parts of the coefficient

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Products of DC Functions on Compact Convex Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constructive product closure for finite DC functions on a compact convex domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty, compact, and convex, and let \(f=g-h\) and \(u=v-w\) with finite convex components. Choose constants so that \(G=g+a\), \(H=h+a\), \(V=v+b\), and \(W=w+b\) are nonnegative on \(K\). For nonnegative convex \(r,s\),
\[
rs=\tfrac12(r+s)^2-\tfrac12r^2-\tfrac12s^2
\]
is a DC representation. Hence
\[
fu=GV+HW-GW-HV
\]
admits a DC decomposition on \(K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The pointwise product of two finite DC functions on a compact convex set is DC; nonnegative shifts of their convex components yield an explicit construction.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty, compact, and convex.
\(g,h,v,w\) are finite convex functions on \(K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((g-h)(v-w)\) is DC on \(K\).
knowledge_statements.title: Products of DC Functions on Compact Convex Sets

knowledge_statements.statement_title: DC representation for a bounded nondecreasing composition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Composite DC representation for a bounded nonnegative DC inner function and a convex nondecreasing outer function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let S\subset\mathbb R^n be compact and convex and let f=f_1-f_2, where f_1,f_2:S\to\mathbb R_+ are convex and 0\leq f(x)\leq a for all x\in S. Let q:[0,a]\to\mathbb R be convex and nondecreasing with q_-'(a)<+\infty, and let K satisfy K\geq |q_-'(a)|. If g is convex and q(f(x))=g(x)-K\bigl(a+f_2(x)-f_1(x)\bigr) for x\in S, then q\circ f is DC on S.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a DC inner function taking values between zero and a, the displayed endpoint-derivative-controlled formula represents its composition with a convex nondecreasing function as a difference of convex functions.
assumptions_latex: S\subset\mathbb R^n\text{ is compact and convex}
f_1,f_2:S\to\mathbb R_+\text{ are convex}
0\leq f(x)\leq a\quad\forall x\in S
q:[0,a]\to\mathbb R\text{ is convex and nondecreasing}
q_-'(a)<+\infty
K\geq |q_-'(a)|
g\text{ is convex and }q(f(x))=g(x)-K\bigl(a+f_2(x)-f_1(x)\bigr)\quad\forall x\in S
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: q\circ f\text{ is DC on }S.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: DC representation for a nonincreasing composition with a nonnegative DC inner function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Composite DC representation using the sum of the convex components of the inner function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let S\subset\mathbb R^n be compact and convex and let f=f_1-f_2, where f_1,f_2:S\to\mathbb R_+ are convex and f(x)\geq 0 for all x\in S. Let q:\mathbb R_+\to\mathbb R be convex and nonincreasing with q_+'(0)>-\infty, and let K>0 satisfy K\geq |q_+'(0)|. If g is convex and q(f(x))=g(x)-K\bigl(f_1(x)+f_2(x)\bigr) for x\in S, then q\circ f is DC on S.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a nonnegative DC inner function represented as the difference of two nonnegative convex functions, the displayed formula represents its composition with the outer function as a difference of convex functions.
assumptions_latex: S\subset\mathbb R^n\text{ is compact and convex}
f_1,f_2:S\to\mathbb R_+\text{ are convex}
f(x)\geq 0\quad\forall x\in S
q:\mathbb R_+\to\mathbb R\text{ is convex and nonincreasing}
q_+'(0)>-\infty
K>0,\quad K\geq |q_+'(0)|
g\text{ is convex and }q(f(x))=g(x)-K\bigl(f_1(x)+f_2(x)\bigr)\quad\forall x\in S

knowledge_statements.statement_title: DC Representation of a Product of Convex Functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic DC decomposition for two convex functions on the nonnegative orthant, under the assumptions stated in the extract.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let f_1,f_2:\mathbb{R}_+^n\to\mathbb{R} be convex. Their product has the DC representation f_1(x)f_2(x)=\frac12\bigl(f_1(x)+f_2(x)\bigr)^2-\frac12\bigl(f_1(x)^2+f_2(x)^2\bigr).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The product of two convex functions on the nonnegative orthant is represented as one half the square of their sum minus one half the sum of their squares.
assumptions_latex: f_1,f_2:\mathbb{R}_+^n\to\mathbb{R}\text{ are convex}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f_1f_2=\frac12(f_1+f_2)^2-\frac12(f_1^2+f_2^2)\text{ is a DC representation}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Spectral-Shift DC Representation of an Indefinite Quadratic
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The spectral-radius bound is sufficient for convexity but may be more conservative than the exact shift threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let Q\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n} be symmetric and indefinite, let f(x)=x^TQx, and let \rho(Q) be the spectral radius of Q. For every \lambda\ge\rho(Q), g(x)=f(x)+\lambda\|x\|^2=x^T(Q+\lambda I)x is convex. Consequently, f(x)=g(x)-\lambda\|x\|^2 is a DC representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A squared-norm shift whose coefficient is at least the spectral radius convexifies the indefinite quadratic and yields a DC decomposition.
assumptions_latex: Q=Q^T\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\text{ is indefinite}
f(x)=x^TQx
\lambda\ge\rho(Q)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: g(x)=f(x)+\lambda\|x\|^2\text{ is convex},\qquad f(x)=g(x)-\lambda\|x\|^2\text{ is DC}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: DC Representation of a Continuous Piecewise-Linear Function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constructive univariate representation using convex functions associated with concave breakpoints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let f:[0,a]\to\mathbb{R} be continuous and piecewise linear with breakpoints 0=c_0<c_1<\cdots<c_k<c_{k+1}=a and U_i=[c_i,c_{i+1}]. Let I be the indices at which f is concave at c_i. For each i\in I, let w_i:[0,a]\to\mathbb{R} be convex, agree with -f on U_i, and be linear on [0,c_i] and [c_i,a]. Then q(x)=\sum_{i\in I}w_i(x), and there is a convex component p=f+q such that f=p-q.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a continuous piecewise-linear function, summing the stated convex extensions associated with concave breakpoints gives the subtractive component of a DC representation.
assumptions_latex: f:[0,a]\to\mathbb{R}\text{ is continuous and piecewise linear}
0=c_0<c_1<\cdots<c_k<c_{k+1}=a
I=\{i:f\text{ is concave at }c_i\}
\forall i\in I,\ w_i\text{ is convex, }w_i=-f\text{ on }U_i\text{, and }w_i\text{ is linear on }[0,c_i]\text{ and }[c_i,a]
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: q=\sum_{i\in I}w_i,\qquad p=f+q\text{ is convex},\qquad f=p-q

knowledge_statements.title: Separable DC Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additively separable functions whose univariate or block components have DC decompositions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C=C_1\times\cdots\times C_m\), where each \(C_i\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n_i}\) is convex. Suppose \(f:C\to\mathbb{R}\) is separable,
\[
f(x_1,\ldots,x_m)=c+\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i),
\]
and each component satisfies \(f_i=g_i-h_i\) with convex \(g_i,h_i:C_i\to\mathbb{R}\). Then
\[
f(x)=\left(c+\sum_{i=1}^m g_i(x_i)\right)-\sum_{i=1}^m h_i(x_i),
\]
where both displayed aggregate functions are convex on \(C\). Thus componentwise DC decompositions combine directly into a DC decomposition of the separable function.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite sum of separable DC components is DC; summing their positive and negative convex parts gives the decomposition.
assumptions_latex: \(C=C_1\times\cdots\times C_m\) with every \(C_i\) convex.
\(f_i=g_i-h_i\) with \(g_i,h_i\) convex and finite on \(C_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f=\left(c+\sum_i g_i\right)-\sum_i h_i\) is DC on \(C\).

notation.meaning: block decomposition of the decision vector

knowledge_statements.title: Polynomial DC Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic convexification of a polynomial restricted to a compact convex set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty, compact, and convex, and let \(p:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be a polynomial. Choose
\[
\rho\ge \max_{x\in K}\max\{0,-\lambda_{\min}(\nabla^2p(x))\}.
\]
Define \(g(x)=p(x)+(\rho/2)\lVert x\rVert_2^2\) and \(h(x)=(\rho/2)\lVert x\rVert_2^2\). Then \(\nabla^2g(x)=\nabla^2p(x)+\rho I\succeq0\) on \(K\), so \(g\) and \(h\) are convex on \(K\), and
\[
p=g-h\quad\text{on }K.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every polynomial restricted to a compact convex set has a DC decomposition obtained by adding and subtracting a sufficiently large quadratic.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty, compact, and convex.
\(p\in\mathbb{R}[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p=g-h\) on \(K\), with \(g\) and \(h\) convex on \(K\).

notation.meaning: smallest eigenvalue of a symmetric matrix

knowledge_statements.statement_title: A Fixed Quadratic Need Not Convexify a Polynomial Globally
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary of the compact-set quadratic convexification construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(p(x)=-x^4\) and any \(\rho\ge0\),
\[
\frac{d^2}{dx^2}\left(p(x)+\frac{\rho}{2}x^2\right)=-12x^2+\rho,
\]
which is negative for sufficiently large \(|x|\). Thus no fixed quadratic shift makes this polynomial convex on all of \(\mathbb{R}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compact-domain quadratic convexification does not extend unchanged to the whole space: negative quartic curvature eventually dominates every fixed quadratic shift.
assumptions_latex: \(p(x)=-x^4\) on \(\mathbb{R}\).
\(\rho\ge0\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p+(\rho/2)x^2\) is not globally convex for any finite \(\rho\).
knowledge_statements.title: A Fixed Quadratic Need Not Convexify a Polynomial Globally

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Global DC Decomposition of Every Polynomial
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Whole-space polynomial DC representation using a higher-degree radial convexifier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(p\in\mathbb{R}[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\). Choose an integer \(d\ge1\) with \(2d>\deg p\), and set \(q_d(x)=(1+\lVert x\rVert_2^2)^d\). There exists \(\rho\ge0\) such that
\[
\nabla^2p(x)+\rho\nabla^2q_d(x)\succeq0\quad\forall x\in\mathbb{R}^n.
\]
Consequently,
\[
p=(p+\rho q_d)-\rho q_d
\]
is a difference of two globally convex polynomials.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every real polynomial is globally DC after adding and subtracting a sufficiently large higher-degree radial convex polynomial.
assumptions_latex: \(p\) is a real polynomial on \(\mathbb{R}^n\).
\(d\) is an integer satisfying \(2d>\deg p\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p\) is the difference of two polynomials convex on all of \(\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.title: Global DC Decomposition of Every Polynomial
Universality of DC Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth universality on compact convex domains, not an unrestricted representation of arbitrary continuous functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty, compact, and convex, and suppose \(f\) is twice continuously differentiable on an open neighborhood of \(K\). Continuity of \(\nabla^2f\) gives a finite \(\rho\ge0\) such that \(\nabla^2f(x)+\rho I\succeq0\) for every \(x\in K\). Consequently,
\[
f(x)=\left(f(x)+\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert x\rVert_2^2\right)-\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert x\rVert_2^2,
\]
and both terms in parentheses are convex on \(K\). Hence every such smooth function is DC on \(K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every twice continuously differentiable function on a neighborhood of a compact convex set is DC on that set.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty, compact, and convex.
\(f\in C^2(U)\) for some open set \(U\supseteq K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\) is representable as a difference of two convex functions on \(K\).

notation.meaning: open neighborhood of the compact domain

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Failure of Unrestricted Continuous and C1 Universality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-dimensional boundary showing that DC universality does not extend to arbitrary continuous or continuously differentiable functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A differentiable function on a compact interval is DC only if its derivative has bounded variation. Consequently, if \(w:[0,1]\to\mathbb{R}\) is continuous with unbounded total variation and
\[
f(x)=\int_0^x w(t)\,dt,
\]
then \(f\in C^1([0,1])\) but \(f\) is not DC on \([0,1]\). In particular, neither continuity nor continuous differentiability alone guarantees a DC representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A C1 function whose derivative has unbounded variation is not DC, so unrestricted C0 or C1 universality is false.
assumptions_latex: \(w:[0,1]\to\mathbb{R}\) is continuous and has unbounded total variation.
knowledge_statements.title: Failure of Unrestricted Continuous and C1 Universality

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic DC representation under a uniform first-order smoothness bound on a convex neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(U\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be open and convex, and let \(f\in C^1(U)\) have an \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient. Then \(x\mapsto f(x)+\frac{L}{2}\lVert x\rVert_2^2\) is convex on \(U\), and
\[
f(x)=\left(f(x)+\frac{L}{2}\lVert x\rVert_2^2\right)-\frac{L}{2}\lVert x\rVert_2^2
\]
is a DC representation on \(U\) and on every convex subset of \(U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A continuously differentiable function with Lipschitz gradient is DC after adding and subtracting a quadratic of matching curvature.
assumptions_latex: \(U\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is open and convex.
\(\lVert\nabla f(x)-\nabla f(y)\rVert_2\le L\lVert x-y\rVert_2\) for all \(x,y\in U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\) is DC on \(U\).
knowledge_statements.title: Lipschitz-Gradient DC Universality

children.title: DC Set Geometry
children.top_down_role: Geometric structure of sets represented through DC constraints.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: DC Representation Does Not Imply Convexity or Connectedness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Elementary intrinsic boundary for the geometry of a set represented by one DC inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
On \(C=\mathbb{R}\), the DC inequality
\[
1-x^2\le0
\]
represents
\[
D=(-\infty,-1]\cup[1,\infty).
\]
Here \(1-x^2=1-(x^2)\) is a difference of finite convex functions, while \(D\) is neither convex nor connected.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even one DC inequality can represent a disconnected, nonconvex set.
assumptions_latex: \(C=\mathbb{R}\).
\(D=\{x\in\mathbb{R}:1-x^2\le0\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D=(-\infty,-1]\cup[1,\infty)\) is DC-represented but neither convex nor connected.
knowledge_statements.title: DC Representation Does Not Imply Convexity or Connectedness

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational finite-inequality convention for DC-represented sets relative to a convex ambient domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be convex. A finite DC-inequality representation of \(D\subseteq C\) is
\[
D=\bigcap_{i=1}^m\{x\in C:g_i(x)-h_i(x)\le0\},
\]
where \(m\) is finite and every \(g_i,h_i:C\to\mathbb{R}\) is finite and convex. The designation concerns the representation, not convexity of \(D\), and the same set may admit many such representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finitely DC-represented set is an intersection of finitely many DC sublevel regions inside a convex ambient domain.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is convex.
\(m\) is finite.
\(g_i,h_i:C\to\mathbb{R}\) are finite convex functions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed family is a finite DC-inequality representation of \(D\) relative to \(C\).
knowledge_statements.title: Finite DC-Inequality Set Representation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Single-Inequality Normal Form and Finite Set Closure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normal form and finite union/intersection closure for the explicitly scoped DC-inequality-represented class.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If
\[
D=\bigcap_{i=1}^m\{x\in C:f_i(x)\le0\}
\]
with finite DC functions \(f_i\), then
\[
D=\{x\in C:\max_{1\le i\le m}f_i(x)\le0\},
\]
and the finite maximum is DC. Consequently, finite intersections of finitely DC-represented sets remain finitely DC-represented. Finite unions do as well: after writing \(D_j=\{x:F_j(x)\le0\}\),
\[
\bigcup_{j=1}^rD_j=\{x\in C:\min_{1\le j\le r}F_j(x)\le0\},
\]
and the finite minimum is DC.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every finite DC constraint system has a single-inequality normal form, and the represented set class is closed under finite intersections and finite unions.
assumptions_latex: All sets use a common convex ambient domain \(C\).
All constraint families and set families are finite.
All constraint functions are finite DC functions on \(C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The finitely DC-inequality-represented subsets of \(C\) are closed under finite intersections and unions.

notation.meaning: single DC constraint representing set j

DC Set Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite inequality representation of a DC set relative to a convex ambient set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be convex. A set \(D\subseteq C\) is called a finitely represented DC set relative to \(C\) if there exist finite convex functions \(g_i,h_i:C\to\mathbb{R}\), for \(i=1,\ldots,m\), such that
\[
D=\bigcap_{i=1}^m\{x\in C:g_i(x)-h_i(x)\le0\}.
\]
The definition concerns the representation of the set; it does not assert that \(D\) itself is convex. Different families of DC inequalities may represent the same geometric set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finitely represented DC set is the intersection, inside a convex ambient set, of finitely many DC sublevel regions.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is convex.
\(m\in\mathbb{N}\) is finite.
\(g_i,h_i:C\to\mathbb{R}\) are finite convex functions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D=\bigcap_i\{x\in C:g_i(x)-h_i(x)\le0\}\) is a DC-set representation relative to \(C\).

children.title: DC Feasible-Region Geometry
children.top_down_role: Feasible-region structure induced by DC program representations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact correspondence between finite DC inequality systems and feasible regions represented relative to a convex ambient domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be convex and let \(f_i=g_i-h_i\), where \(g_i,h_i:C\to\mathbb{R}\) are finite convex functions. The feasible region of the finite DC system \(f_i(x)\le0\) is
\[
F=C\cap\bigcap_{i=1}^m\{x:g_i(x)-h_i(x)\le0\}.
\]
Conversely, every subset of \(C\) supplied with such a finite DC-inequality representation is the feasible region of a canonical DC constraint system. This is a representation correspondence and imposes no convexity or connectedness on \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite DC inequality descriptions and feasible regions of canonical DC constraint systems are the same represented objects relative to a convex ambient domain.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is convex.
\(m\) is finite.
\(g_i,h_i:C\to\mathbb{R}\) are finite convex functions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\) is exactly the feasible region represented by the finite DC inequality family.
knowledge_statements.title: DC Constraint–Feasible-Region Correspondence
DC Feasible-Region Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correspondence between finite DC-set descriptions and feasible regions of canonical DC inequality systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be convex and let \(f_i=g_i-h_i\), where \(g_i,h_i:C\to\mathbb{R}\) are convex. The feasible region of the system \(f_i(x)\le0\), for \(i=1,\ldots,m\), is exactly
\[
F=C\cap\bigcap_{i=1}^m\{x:g_i(x)-h_i(x)\le0\}.
\]
Conversely, every finitely represented DC set relative to \(C\) is the feasible region of such a finite DC inequality system. Thus finite DC-set geometry and canonical DC feasibility descriptions coincide at the level of represented subsets of \(C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite DC inequality systems generate precisely the finitely represented DC sets in a convex ambient domain.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is convex.
\(g_i,h_i:C\to\mathbb{R}\) are finite convex functions for finitely many indices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\) is a finitely represented DC set, and every such set arises as a DC feasible region.

children.title: DC Set-to-Program Encodings
children.top_down_role: Routes connecting DC set descriptions to optimization-model feasible regions.

knowledge_statements.title: DC Set-to-Program Encodings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact continuous minimization encoding of feasibility for a finite DC inequality description on a compact convex domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty, compact, and convex, and let \(D=\{x\in C:g_i(x)-h_i(x)\le0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\), where all \(g_i,h_i:C\to\mathbb{R}\) are continuous and convex. Define
\[
\Phi(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m[g_i(x)-h_i(x)]_+,
\qquad [g_i-h_i]_+=\max\{g_i,h_i\}-h_i.
\]
Then \(\Phi\) is continuous, DC, and nonnegative on \(C\), and
\[
D\ne\varnothing\iff\min_{x\in C}\Phi(x)=0,
\qquad D=\{x\in C:\Phi(x)=0\}.
\]
Thus set membership and feasibility are encoded exactly by a DC penalty program.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a compact convex domain, summed positive violations of continuous DC constraints form a continuous nonnegative DC objective whose zero minimizers are exactly the feasible points.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty, compact, and convex.
\(g_i,h_i:C\to\mathbb{R}\) are continuous convex functions for \(i=1,\ldots,m\).
\(m\in\mathbb{N}\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D\ne\varnothing\) exactly when \(\min_{x\in C}\Phi(x)=0\), and \(D=\{x\in C:\Phi(x)=0\}\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of the zero-optimum feasibility test when the violation objective need not attain its infimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Compactness or another attainment hypothesis is essential for the implication \(\inf_C\Phi=0\Rightarrow D\ne\varnothing\). Let \(C=\mathbb{R}\), impose \(e^x\le0\), and set \(\Phi(x)=[e^x]_+=e^x\). Then
\[
D=\varnothing,
\qquad
\inf_{x\in\mathbb{R}}\Phi(x)=0.
\]
For an arbitrary domain, the pointwise identity \(D=\{x:\Phi(x)=0\}\) remains valid even when the zero-infimum test fails.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without attainment, an infeasible DC system can have violation infimum zero; only the zero-level-set identity remains unconditional.
assumptions_latex: \(C=\mathbb{R}\).
\(D=\{x\in\mathbb{R}:e^x\le0\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D=\varnothing\) and \(\inf_{x\in C}\Phi(x)=0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Noncompact Zero-Infimum Failure

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional constrained minimization in an explicitly scoped convex-difference objective and inequality convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Relative to a convex domain \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), a canonical DC program has the form
\[
\inf_{x\in C}\{g_0(x)-h_0(x):g_i(x)-h_i(x)\le0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\},
\]
where \(g_i,h_i:C\to\mathbb{R}\) are finite convex functions. Equivalently, the objective can be epigraphed as
\[
\inf_{(x,t)\in C\times\mathbb{R}}t
\quad\text{subject to}\quad
 g_0(x)-h_0(x)-t\le0,
\quad g_i(x)-h_i(x)\le0.
\]
This convention concerns model representation and does not imply that the feasible region is convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A canonical DC program minimizes a convex difference over a convex domain subject to finitely many convex-difference inequalities; its objective also has an exact epigraph DC encoding.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is convex.
\(m\) is finite.
\(g_i,h_i:C\to\mathbb{R}\) are finite convex functions for \(i=0,\ldots,m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed formulations are equivalent canonical DC programs.
knowledge_statements.title: Canonical DC Program Form
Canonical DC Programs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional constrained minimization in standard difference-of-convex form.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A canonical DC program on a convex set \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) has the form
\[
\inf_{x\in C}\{g_0(x)-h_0(x):g_i(x)-h_i(x)\le0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\},
\]
where every \(g_i,h_i:C\to\mathbb{R}\) is convex and finite, including the objective pair indexed by \(0\). The feasible set may be nonconvex because subtracting \(h_i\) need not preserve convex sublevel geometry. A feasible point attaining the infimum, when one exists, is a global solution if its objective value is no larger than that of every other feasible point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A canonical DC program minimizes one convex difference over a convex domain subject to finitely many convex-difference inequalities.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is convex.
\(g_i,h_i:C\to\mathbb{R}\) are finite convex functions for \(i=0,\ldots,m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed optimization problem is in canonical DC form.

knowledge_statements.title: Noncanonical DC Programs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact reductions of common equality, maximum, and disjunctive DC constraints to canonical inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let all functions below be DC on a common convex domain \(C\). A DC equality \(f(x)=0\) is equivalent to the pair \(f(x)\le0\) and \(-f(x)\le0\). A finite maximum constraint satisfies
\[
\max_{1\le k\le r}f_k(x)\le0\iff f_k(x)\le0\quad(k=1,\ldots,r).
\]
A finite disjunction satisfies
\[
\bigvee_{k=1}^r[f_k(x)\le0]
\iff \min_{1\le k\le r}f_k(x)\le0.
\]
Because negation and finite minima preserve the DC class, these noncanonical constraint forms have exact canonical DC inequality encodings without changing their feasible points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: DC equalities, finite maximum constraints, and finite disjunctions admit exact reformulations using canonical DC inequalities.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is convex.
\(f,f_1,\ldots,f_r:C\to\mathbb{R}\) are finite DC functions.
\(r\in\mathbb{N}\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed transformations preserve the feasible set and yield canonical DC inequalities.

children.title: Partly Convex Models
children.top_down_role: Models retaining convex structure in selected variables or components.

knowledge_statements.title: Partly Convex Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Blockwise convexity with respect to designated variables, including the biconvex two-block specialization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^p\) and \(Y\subseteq\mathbb{R}^q\) be convex. A function \(f:X\times Y\to\mathbb{R}\) is convex in the \(x\)-block if \(x\mapsto f(x,y)\) is convex on \(X\) for every fixed \(y\in Y\). A model is partly convex when its objective or designated constraint functions possess convexity in at least one specified variable block while the remaining blocks are fixed. If both \(x\mapsto f(x,y)\) and \(y\mapsto f(x,y)\) are convex for every fixed complementary block, then \(f\) is biconvex. Blockwise convexity does not by itself imply joint convexity on \(X\times Y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A partly convex model is convex in designated variable blocks with all complementary blocks fixed; biconvexity requires this for both blocks.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^p\) and \(Y\subseteq\mathbb{R}^q\) are convex.
\(f:X\times Y\to\mathbb{R}\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Convexity of the indicated partial mappings defines partial or biconvex structure, not necessarily joint convexity.

children.title: Convex–Concave Models
children.top_down_role: Models organized around interacting convex and concave components.

knowledge_statements.title: Convex–Concave Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-block saddle models with convex minimizing sections and concave maximizing sections.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^p\) and \(Y\subseteq\mathbb{R}^q\) be convex. A function \(L:X\times Y\to\mathbb{R}\) is convex–concave when \(x\mapsto L(x,y)\) is convex on \(X\) for every \(y\in Y\), and \(y\mapsto L(x,y)\) is concave on \(Y\) for every \(x\in X\). The associated saddle model is
\[
\inf_{x\in X}\sup_{y\in Y}L(x,y).
\]
A pair \((x^*,y^*)\in X\times Y\) is a saddle point when
\[
L(x^*,y)\le L(x^*,y^*)\le L(x,y^*)
\]
for every \(x\in X\) and \(y\in Y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex–concave model is convex in its minimizing block and concave in its maximizing block; saddle points satisfy the two-sided saddle inequality.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^p\) and \(Y\subseteq\mathbb{R}^q\) are convex.
\(L:X\times Y\to\mathbb{R}\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The partial convexity and concavity conditions define the displayed saddle model and saddle-point predicate.

source_refs.locator: 9.3.1 Biconvex and Convex-Concave Programming p. 190

source_witnesses.locator: 9.3.1 Biconvex and Convex-Concave Programming p. 190

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact nonnegative gap test and epsilon residual for a candidate saddle pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \((x,y)\in X\times Y\), suppose the following quantities are finite and define
\[
G(x,y)=\sup_{v\in Y}L(x,v)-\inf_{u\in X}L(u,y).
\]
Then \(G(x,y)\ge0\), and
\[
G(x,y)=0
\iff
L(x,v)\le L(x,y)\le L(u,y)
\quad(\forall u\in X,\ \forall v\in Y).
\]
Thus zero gap is equivalent to the saddle-point condition, while \(G(x,y)\le\varepsilon\) bounds the sum of the two unilateral saddle residuals by \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The saddle gap is nonnegative, vanishes exactly at saddle points, and provides an epsilon saddle residual.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(Y\) are nonempty.
\(L(x,y)\) is finite at the candidate pair.
The displayed supremum and infimum are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G(x,y)=0\iff(x,y)\) is a saddle point.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal–Dual Gap Saddle Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Minimax Equality Can Fail Without Compactness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Noncompact convex–concave example with a strict extended-valued minimax gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X=Y=(0,\infty)\) and \(L(x,y)=yx^2-x\). Each map \(L(\cdot,y)\) is convex and each map \(L(x,\cdot)\) is affine and hence concave, but
\[
\inf_{x>0}\sup_{y>0}L(x,y)=+\infty,
\qquad
\sup_{y>0}\inf_{x>0}L(x,y)=0.
\]
Therefore sectional convex–concavity alone does not imply minimax equality, finite minimax value, or saddle-point existence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On noncompact blocks, a finite convex–concave function can have a strict minimax gap and no saddle point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_X\sup_YL=+\infty>0=\sup_Y\inf_XL\).
knowledge_statements.title: Minimax Equality Can Fail Without Compactness

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional compact continuous minimax equality and saddle-point existence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^p\) and \(Y\subseteq\mathbb{R}^q\) be nonempty compact convex sets. If \(L:X\times Y\to\mathbb{R}\) is continuous, convex in \(x\) for every fixed \(y\), and concave in \(y\) for every fixed \(x\), then
\[
\min_{x\in X}\max_{y\in Y}L(x,y)=\max_{y\in Y}\min_{x\in X}L(x,y).
\]
Both extrema are attained, and every minimax optimizer paired with every maximin optimizer is a saddle point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A continuous convex–concave function on compact convex blocks has equal attained minimax and maximin values and a saddle point.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(Y\) are nonempty compact convex subsets of finite-dimensional spaces.
\(L\) is continuous on \(X\times Y\).
\(L(\cdot,y)\) is convex and \(L(x,\cdot)\) is concave.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{x\in X}\max_{y\in Y}L(x,y)=\max_{y\in Y}\min_{x\in X}L(x,y)\), with saddle-point attainment.
knowledge_statements.title: Compact Continuous Convex–Concave Minimax Theorem

children.title: Partial-Convexity Representation Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Structural limits separating partial-convexity forms from general DC representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Partial-Convexity Representation Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Blockwise convexity is strictly weaker than joint convexity, even for smooth bilinear functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
On \(X=Y=[-1,1]\), define \(f(x,y)=xy\). For every fixed \(y\), the mapping \(x\mapsto xy\) is affine and hence convex; likewise, for every fixed \(x\), the mapping \(y\mapsto xy\) is affine and convex. Thus \(f\) is biconvex. However,
\[
\nabla^2 f(x,y)=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}
\]
has eigenvalues \(-1\) and \(1\), so \(f\) is neither jointly convex nor jointly concave on \([-1,1]^2\). Therefore partial or separate convexity cannot be substituted for joint convexity in convex-model representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The bilinear function is convex in each variable separately but neither convex nor concave jointly, marking the boundary of partial-convexity claims.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Separate convexity of \(f\) does not imply joint convexity or joint concavity on \(X\times Y\).

children.title: DC Optimality-Duality Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Global criteria and dual constructions are grouped after representation because both depend on the selected DC decomposition.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact DC Global Optimality Criteria
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact objective-difference criterion for a finite-dimensional constrained DC minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty and convex, and let \(g,h:C\to\mathbb{R}\) be convex. For \(f=g-h\) and \(\bar x\in C\), the following condition is necessary and sufficient for global optimality:
\[
\bar x\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C} f(x)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
g(x)-g(\bar x)\ge h(x)-h(\bar x)\quad\text{for every }x\in C.
\]
Equivalently, the convex increment of \(g\) from \(\bar x\) dominates the convex increment of \(h\) at every feasible point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible point globally minimizes a DC objective exactly when every feasible increment of its first convex component dominates the corresponding increment of its second component.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty and convex.
\(g\) and \(h\) are finite convex functions on \(C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar x\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}(g(x)-h(x))\) exactly under the displayed increment inequality.

source_refs.locator: 2.6 Difference of Convex (D.C.) Functions p. 58

source_witnesses.locator: 2.6 Difference of Convex (D.C.) Functions p. 58

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact global DC optimality characterized by epsilon-subdifferential inclusion for finite convex components.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(g,h:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be finite convex functions and \(\bar x\in\mathbb{R}^n\). For \(\varepsilon\ge0\), let
\[
\partial_\varepsilon q(\bar x)=\{y:q(x)\ge q(\bar x)+\langle y,x-\bar x\rangle-\varepsilon\ \forall x\in\mathbb{R}^n\}.
\]
Then
\[
\bar x\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}(g-h)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\partial_\varepsilon h(\bar x)\subseteq\partial_\varepsilon g(\bar x)\quad\forall\varepsilon\ge0.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A point globally minimizes a finite-valued DC function exactly when every epsilon-subgradient of the subtracted component is an epsilon-subgradient of the first component for every nonnegative epsilon.
assumptions_latex: \(g,h:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) are finite convex functions.
\(\bar x\in\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar x\in\operatorname*{argmin}(g-h)\) exactly under the all-epsilon inclusions.
knowledge_statements.title: All-Epsilon DC Inclusion Criterion

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Ordinary Common Subgradients Do Not Certify Global DC Optimality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of replacing all-epsilon inclusion by ordinary common-subgradient stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
On \(\mathbb{R}\), let \(g(x)=0\) and \(h(x)=x^2\). At \(\bar x=0\),
\[
\partial g(0)=\partial h(0)=\{0\},
\]
but \((g-h)(x)=-x^2\) is unbounded below. Thus a common ordinary subgradient does not imply global optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A common ordinary subgradient is only a criticality condition: for zero minus x-squared it holds at zero although the DC objective is unbounded below.
assumptions_latex: \(g(x)=0\) and \(h(x)=x^2\) on \(\mathbb{R}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\partial g(0)\cap\partial h(0)\ne\varnothing\) does not imply \(0\in\operatorname*{argmin}(g-h)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Ordinary Common Subgradients Do Not Certify Global DC Optimality
DC Inclusion Criteria
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global optimality expressed through all approximate subdifferentials of the convex components.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Extend \(g\) and \(h\) by \(+\infty\) outside the closed convex feasible set \(C\). For \(\varepsilon\ge0\), define
\[
\partial_\varepsilon q(\bar x)=\{y:q(x)\ge q(\bar x)+\langle y,x-\bar x\rangle-\varepsilon\ \text{for every }x\in\mathbb{R}^n\}.
\]
If \(g,h\) are proper lower-semicontinuous convex functions and \(\bar x\in\operatorname{dom}g\cap\operatorname{dom}h\), then
\[
\bar x\in\operatorname*{argmin}(g-h)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\partial_\varepsilon h(\bar x)\subseteq\partial_\varepsilon g(\bar x)
\quad\text{for every }\varepsilon\ge0.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible point is globally DC-optimal exactly when every epsilon-subgradient of the subtracted convex component is an epsilon-subgradient of the first component, for every epsilon.
assumptions_latex: \(g,h:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) are proper lower-semicontinuous convex functions.
\(\bar x\in\operatorname{dom}g\cap\operatorname{dom}h\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar x\) is globally optimal if and only if \(\partial_\varepsilon h(\bar x)\subseteq\partial_\varepsilon g(\bar x)\) for every \(\varepsilon\ge0\).

A source giving the exact theorem and its domain assumptions is required.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive global near-optimality for finite convex DC components, characterized by shifted epsilon-subdifferential inclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(g,h:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be finite convex functions, \(\bar x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and \(\delta\ge0\). Define \(\partial_\varepsilon q(\bar x)=\{y:q(x)\ge q(\bar x)+\langle y,x-\bar x\rangle-\varepsilon\ \forall x\}\). Then
\[
g(\bar x)-h(\bar x)\le \inf_x(g(x)-h(x))+\delta
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\partial_\varepsilon h(\bar x)\subseteq\partial_{\varepsilon+\delta}g(\bar x)\quad\forall\varepsilon\ge0.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A point is globally optimal within additive delta exactly when every epsilon-subgradient of the subtracted convex component is an epsilon-plus-delta subgradient of the first component.
assumptions_latex: \(g,h:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) are finite convex functions.
\(\bar x\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(\delta\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g(\bar x)-h(\bar x)\le\inf(g-h)+\delta\) exactly under the displayed shifted inclusions.
knowledge_statements.title: Additive Approximate DC Inclusion Criterion
Approximate DC Global Optimality Criteria
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive approximate global optimality characterized by relaxed epsilon-subdifferential inclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(g,h:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper lower-semicontinuous convex functions, and let \(\bar x\in\operatorname{dom}g\cap\operatorname{dom}h\). For a tolerance \(\delta\ge0\),
\[
g(\bar x)-h(\bar x)\le\inf_x\{g(x)-h(x)\}+\delta
\]
holds if and only if
\[
\partial_\varepsilon h(\bar x)
\subseteq
\partial_{\varepsilon+\delta}g(\bar x)
\quad\text{for every }\varepsilon\ge0.
\]
Thus the additive enlargement in the receiving subdifferential equals the permitted global objective error.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Delta-global optimality is equivalent to placing every epsilon-subgradient of the subtracted component inside the epsilon-plus-delta subdifferential of the first component.
assumptions_latex: \(g\) and \(h\) are proper lower-semicontinuous convex functions.
\(\bar x\in\operatorname{dom}g\cap\operatorname{dom}h\) and \(\delta\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g(\bar x)-h(\bar x)\le\inf(g-h)+\delta\) exactly under the displayed relaxed inclusions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal and Fenchel-conjugate DC minimization families for finite convex components.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(g,h:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be finite convex functions. Define
\[
(P)\quad\inf_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\{g(x)-h(x)\},
\qquad
(D)\quad\inf_{y\in\operatorname{dom}h^*}\{h^*(y)-g^*(y)\}.
\]
Then their values agree in the extended-real sense:
\[
\inf(P)=\inf(D).
\]
If \(y\in\partial g(x)\cap\partial h(x)\), their objective values agree at that pair:
\[
g(x)-h(x)=h^*(y)-g^*(y).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite-valued DC minimization problem and its reversed-conjugate DC problem have the same extended optimal value; common subgradients match their objective values.
assumptions_latex: \(g,h:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) are finite convex functions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_x(g-h)=\inf_{y\in\operatorname{dom}h^*}(h^*-g^*)\), with paired equality at common subgradients.

notation.meaning: primal and conjugate-dual DC problem families

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Valued Toland Conjugate Pair
DC Primal-Dual Problem Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Toland–Singer conjugate pairing for unconstrained DC programs, including constraints through indicator functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For proper lower-semicontinuous convex functions \(g,h:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\), the DC primal and conjugate dual families are
\[
(P)\quad \inf_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\{g(x)-h(x)\},
\qquad
(D)\quad \inf_{y\in\mathbb{R}^n}\{h^*(y)-g^*(y)\}.
\]
Whenever Toland–Singer duality applies, their optimal values coincide. Moreover, if \(y\in\partial g(x)\cap\partial h(x)\), Fenchel equalities give
\[
g(x)-h(x)=h^*(y)-g^*(y).
\]
A constrained problem on a closed convex set \(C\) is included by replacing \(g\) with \(g+\iota_C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A DC minimization problem has a conjugate DC dual obtained by reversing the conjugates; common subgradients identify equal primal and dual objective values.
assumptions_latex: \(g\) and \(h\) are proper lower-semicontinuous convex functions.
The relevant primal and dual values are finite and the stated Toland–Singer qualification holds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf(g-h)=\inf(h^*-g^*)\), with equal paired objective values at common subgradients.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The duality role fits the container, but “whenever Toland–Singer duality applies” is not an explicit hypothesis. The exact domain or qualification conditions supporting equality of the two infima require a specific theorem citation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of exact support recovery without lower semicontinuity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define \(f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}\) by \(f(x)=0\) for \(x>0\) and \(f(x)=1\) for \(x\le0\). Then \(f\) is quasiconvex but not lower-semicontinuous, and
\[
\{x:f(x)\le0\}=(0,\infty).
\]
The intersection of all closed halfspaces containing this sublevel set is \([0,\infty)\), so its support values recover the closure rather than the original sublevel set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without lower semicontinuity, support-halfspace reconstruction can close a nonclosed quasiconvex sublevel set and fail to recover the function exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Support-function reconstruction need not recover a nonclosed quasiconvex sublevel set.
knowledge_statements.title: Loss of Nonclosed Quasiconvex Sublevels

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A specified support-function convention for representing lower-semicontinuous quasiconvex functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper, lower-semicontinuous, and quasiconvex. For \(\alpha\in\mathbb{R}\), define
\[
Q_f(y,\alpha)=\sup\{\langle y,z\rangle:f(z)\le\alpha\},
\]
with \(\sup\varnothing=-\infty\). Then
\[
\{x:f(x)\le\alpha\}=\bigcap_{y\in\mathbb{R}^n}\{x:\langle y,x\rangle\le Q_f(y,\alpha)\},
\]
and
\[
f(x)=\inf\{\alpha\in\mathbb{R}:\langle y,x\rangle\le Q_f(y,\alpha)\ \forall y\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the stated convention, a lower-semicontinuous quasiconvex function is recovered from the support functions of its closed convex sublevel sets.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, lower-semicontinuous, and quasiconvex.
The convention \(\sup\varnothing=-\infty\) is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every sublevel set, and hence \(f\), is recovered from \(Q_f\).

notation.meaning: support function of the alpha-sublevel set

knowledge_statements.title: Level-Set Support Quasiconjugacy
Quasiconjugate Duality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Level-set support quasiconjugacy for proper lower-semicontinuous quasiconvex functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper, lower-semicontinuous, and quasiconvex. Define its level-set quasiconjugate by
\[
Q_f(y,\alpha)=\sup\{\langle y,x\rangle:f(x)\le\alpha\}.
\]
Every nonempty sublevel set is recovered from these values as
\[
\{x:f(x)\le\alpha\}
=
\bigcap_{y\in\mathbb{R}^n}
\{x:\langle y,x\rangle\le Q_f(y,\alpha)\}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
f(x)=\inf\{\alpha:\langle y,x\rangle\le Q_f(y,\alpha)\ \text{for every }y\in\mathbb{R}^n\},
\]
with the infimum interpreted in the extended-real sense.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lower-semicontinuous quasiconvex function is represented by the support functions of its convex sublevel sets, yielding a level-set form of quasiconjugate duality.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, lower-semicontinuous, and quasiconvex.
The represented sublevel set is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The sublevel sets, and hence \(f\), are recovered from \(Q_f\).

notation.meaning: support-function quasiconjugate of the alpha-sublevel set

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The support representation of closed convex sublevel sets is mathematically plausible, but quasiconjugate conventions vary and no source is supplied for this definition or recovery formula.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact primal optimality certified by an attained conjugate-dual value and Fenchel equalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(g,h:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be finite convex functions, and consider
\[
(P)=\inf_x\{g(x)-h(x)\},\qquad (D)=\inf_{y\in\operatorname{dom}h^*}\{h^*(y)-g^*(y)\}.
\]
If \(\bar y\) globally minimizes \((D)\) and
\[
\bar y\in\partial g(\bar x)\cap\partial h(\bar x),
\]
then
\[
g(\bar x)-h(\bar x)=h^*(\bar y)-g^*(\bar y)=\inf(P),
\]
so \(\bar x\) is a global primal minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A globally optimal conjugate-dual point sharing both convex subgradients with a primal point certifies exact primal global optimality and zero conjugate gap.
assumptions_latex: \(g,h:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) are finite convex functions.
\(\bar y\) attains the conjugate-dual infimum.
\(\bar y\in\partial g(\bar x)\cap\partial h(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar x\in\operatorname*{argmin}(g-h)\) and the displayed primal and dual values coincide.
knowledge_statements.title: Common-Subgradient DC Dual Certificate
DC Dual-Bound Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global optimality certificate formed by a conjugate-dual minimizer and Fenchel equality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider the Toland pair \((P)\) and \((D)\) for proper lower-semicontinuous convex \(g,h\), under equality of their finite optimal values. A pair \((\bar x,\bar y)\) certifies global primal optimality if
\[
\bar y\in\partial g(\bar x)\cap\partial h(\bar x)
\quad\text{and}\quad
h^*(\bar y)-g^*(\bar y)
\le h^*(y)-g^*(y)
\quad\text{for every }y.
\]
The common-subgradient relations are directly checked by Fenchel equalities, and they imply
\[
g(\bar x)-h(\bar x)=h^*(\bar y)-g^*(\bar y)=\inf(P).
\]
Thus the dual optimum and zero conjugate gap certify the primal bound exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dual global minimizer sharing both convex subgradients with a primal point certifies that point’s global DC optimality through zero conjugate gap.
assumptions_latex: Toland duality holds with a finite common optimal value.
\(g\) and \(h\) are proper lower-semicontinuous convex functions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar x\in\operatorname*{argmin}(g-h)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Convex Minorants of DC Functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex lower bounds obtained from concave majorization of the subtracted component.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f=g-h\) on a convex set \(C\), where \(g,h:C\to\mathbb{R}\) are convex. If \(U:C\to\mathbb{R}\) is concave and satisfies \(U(x)\ge h(x)\) for every \(x\in C\), then
\[
m_U(x)=g(x)-U(x)
\]
is convex on \(C\) and obeys
\[
m_U(x)\le f(x)\quad\text{for every }x\in C.
\]
Consequently,
\[
\inf_{x\in C}m_U(x)\le\inf_{x\in C}f(x),
\]
so minimizing \(m_U\) supplies a valid global lower bound for the DC problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Subtracting any concave upper estimator of the second convex component from the first component produces a convex minorant and a valid global lower bound.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is convex and nonempty.
\(g\) and \(h\) are convex on \(C\).
\(U\) is concave on \(C\) and majorizes \(h\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m_U=g-U\) is convex, \(m_U\le g-h\), and \(\inf_Cm_U\le\inf_C(g-h)\).

notation.meaning: induced convex minorant of the DC objective

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Contact and Exactness of a Majorant-Induced Minorant
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise gap identity and a sufficient exact-bound certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f=g-h\) and \(m_U=g-U\) on \(C\), where \(U\ge h\). Then \[f(x)-m_U(x)=U(x)-h(x)\ge0.\] Thus \(m_U(x)=f(x)\) exactly when \(U(x)=h(x)\). If some \(x^\star\) minimizes both \(f\) and \(m_U\) and satisfies \(U(x^\star)=h(x^\star)\), then \(\min_Cm_U=\min_Cf\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The minorant gap equals the majorant gap. Contact gives pointwise exactness, and contact at a common minimizer certifies an exact lower bound.
assumptions_latex: \(U\) is a concave majorant of \(h\) on \(C\).
For optimal-value exactness, \(x^\star\) minimizes both \(f\) and \(m_U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f-m_U=U-h,\qquad U(x)=h(x)\iff m_U(x)=f(x).

notation.meaning: common minimizer used by the exactness certificate

knowledge_statements.title: Contact and Exactness of a Majorant-Induced Minorant

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise strongest member of the family induced by concave majorants of the subtracted component.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty, compact, and convex, and let \(f=g-h\), where \(g,h\) are finite convex functions and \(h\) is continuous on \(C\). Define \[\operatorname{cav}_C h(x)=\sup\left\{\sum_{i=1}^r\lambda_i h(x_i):\lambda_i\ge0,\ \sum_i\lambda_i=1,\ \sum_i\lambda_i x_i=x,\ x_i\in C\right\}.\] This is the least concave majorant of \(h\) on \(C\). Hence \(m^*=g-\operatorname{cav}_C h\) is convex and, for every concave majorant \(U\ge h\), \[g-U\le m^*\le g-h\quad\text{on }C.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a fixed DC decomposition on a compact convex set, subtracting the least concave majorant of the second component gives the pointwise strongest minorant obtainable by this construction.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, compact, and convex.
\(g\) and \(h\) are finite convex functions on \(C\).
\(h\) is continuous on \(C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: g-U\le g-\operatorname{cav}_C h\le g-h\quad\text{for every concave }U\ge h.

notation.meaning: least concave majorant of h on C

knowledge_statements.title: Strongest Fixed-Decomposition Majorant Minorant
Polyhedral DC Underestimators
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simplexwise polyhedral underestimation using vertex interpolation of the subtracted convex component.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S=\operatorname{conv}\{v_0,\ldots,v_n\}\) be a simplex and write each \(x\in S\) uniquely as \(x=\sum_{i=0}^n\lambda_i(x)v_i\), where \(\lambda_i(x)\ge0\) and \(\sum_i\lambda_i(x)=1\). For convex \(h\), define
\[
U_S(x)=\sum_{i=0}^n\lambda_i(x)h(v_i).
\]
Convexity gives \(h(x)\le U_S(x)\). Hence, for \(f=g-h\),
\[
m_S(x)=g(x)-U_S(x)\le f(x)\quad(x\in S).
\]
The function \(U_S\) is affine; if \(g\) is polyhedral convex, then \(m_S\) is a polyhedral convex underestimator on \(S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Vertex interpolation upper-bounds the subtracted convex component on a simplex, producing a valid underestimator that is polyhedral convex when the first component is polyhedral convex.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is a nondegenerate simplex.
\(g\) and \(h\) are convex and finite on \(S\).
\(g\) is polyhedral when polyhedrality of \(m_S\) is asserted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m_S=g-U_S\le g-h\) on \(S\), and \(m_S\) is polyhedral convex when \(g\) is polyhedral convex.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Approximation properties of piecewise-affine vertex-interpolation DC underestimators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) be a compact polytope, let \(h:P\to\mathbb R\) be continuous and convex, and let \(\mathcal T'\) be a conforming refinement of a finite triangulation \(\mathcal T\). If \(U_{\mathcal T}\) and \(U_{\mathcal T'}\) are the piecewise-affine vertex interpolants of \(h\), then \(h\le U_{\mathcal T'}\le U_{\mathcal T}\) on \(P\). Thus, for \(f=g-h\), \(g-U_{\mathcal T}\le g-U_{\mathcal T'}\le f\). For triangulations \(\mathcal T_k\) whose maximum simplex diameter tends to zero, \(\|U_{\mathcal T_k}-h\|_\infty\to0\), and hence \(\|f-(g-U_{\mathcal T_k})\|_\infty\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conforming refinement monotonically strengthens vertex-interpolation underestimators, and vanishing mesh makes them uniformly exact.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is a compact polytope.
\(h\) is finite, continuous, and convex on \(P\).
Monotonicity uses a conforming refinement; consistency uses maximum simplex diameter tending to zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The refined underestimator dominates the coarse one, and vanishing mesh yields uniform convergence to \(f\).

notation.meaning: piecewise-affine vertex interpolant on triangulation \(\mathcal T\)

knowledge_statements.title: Monotone Refinement and Uniform Consistency
Decomposition-Dependent Lower Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity is decomposition invariant, but numerical strength depends on the chosen DC decomposition and majorant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose the same objective has two DC decompositions
\[
f=g-h=(g+\phi)-(h+\phi),
\]
where \(g,h,\phi\) are convex on \(C\). Let \(U\ge h\) and \(\widetilde U\ge h+\phi\) be concave majorants on \(C\). Their valid lower bounds are
\[
L=\inf_{x\in C}\{g(x)-U(x)\},
\qquad
\widetilde L=\inf_{x\in C}\{g(x)+\phi(x)-\widetilde U(x)\}.
\]
Both satisfy \(L,\widetilde L\le\inf_C f\), but neither ordering \(L\le\widetilde L\) nor \(\widetilde L\le L\) follows without an ordering between \(U\) and \(\widetilde U-\phi\). Thus bound strength is decomposition dependent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding the same convex function to both DC components preserves the objective but can strengthen or weaken lower bounds because the required majorant changes.
assumptions_latex: \(g,h,\phi\) are convex on a nonempty convex set \(C\).
\(U\) and \(\widetilde U\) are the stated concave majorants.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Both bounds are valid, while their relative strength requires comparing \(U\) with \(\widetilde U-\phi\).

notation.meaning: lower bounds from two DC decompositions
convex function added to both components

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit failure of any decomposition-independent ordering of valid DC lower bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(C=[0,1]\), let \(f\equiv0\). For \(f=0-0\), the concave majorant \(U\equiv1\) gives \(L=-1\). For the equivalent decomposition \(f=x^2-x^2\), the affine secant majorant \(\widetilde U(x)=x\) gives \(\widetilde L=\min_{[0,1]}(x^2-x)=-1/4>L\). Replacing \(U\) by the valid majorant \(U\equiv0\) gives \(L=0>\widetilde L\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equivalent DC decompositions can yield either ordering of their valid lower bounds, depending on the selected majorants.
assumptions_latex: Each selected majorant is concave and pointwise dominates the corresponding subtracted convex component.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Neither ordering between decomposition-dependent lower bounds holds without an estimator comparison.

notation.meaning: majorants associated with the two decompositions

knowledge_statements.title: Reversal of Decomposition-Bound Strength
Canonical DC Outer Approximation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cutting-plane lower approximation built from valid convex minorants of a DC objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Input a compact convex set \(C\), a DC objective \(f=g-h\), a tolerance \(\tau\ge0\), and an oracle producing concave majorants \(U_k\ge h\) on \(C\). Initialize a feasible incumbent \(x^0\) and \(B^0=f(x^0)\). At iteration \(k\), form \(m_k=g-U_k\) and solve
\[
L_k=\min_{x\in C,\,t}\{t:t\ge m_j(x),\ j=1,\ldots,k\}.
\]
Evaluate a feasible trial point \(x^k\), update \(B^k=\min\{B^{k-1},f(x^k)\}\), and stop when \(B^k-L_k\le\tau\). Otherwise generate \(U_{k+1}\) and repeat. The output is \(\tau\)-globally optimal whenever \(L_k\) is valid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method accumulates convex minorant cuts, solves their epigraph master for a lower bound, updates a feasible incumbent, and stops when the global gap meets tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is nonempty and compact.
Each oracle output \(U_k\) is concave and satisfies \(U_k\ge h\) on \(C\).
The master and trial-point subproblems are solved to the declared accuracy.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Termination with \(B^k-L_k\le\tau\) returns an incumbent whose objective is within \(\tau\) of the global optimum.

knowledge_statements.title: Outer-Approximation Master Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Epigraph master combining accumulated regional or global convex minorants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C_k\subseteq C\) be the current search region and let \(m_1,\ldots,m_k\) be convex functions satisfying \(m_j(x)\le f(x)\) on \(C_k\). The outer-approximation master is
\[
L_k=\begin{aligned}[t]
\min_{x,t}&\quad t\\
\text{subject to}&\quad x\in C_k,\\
&\quad t\ge m_j(x),\qquad j=1,\ldots,k.
\end{aligned}
\]
Equivalently, \(L_k=\min_{x\in C_k}\max_{j\le k}m_j(x)\). Since the pointwise maximum remains below \(f\),
\[
L_k\le\inf_{x\in C_k}f(x).
\]
Adding a valid cut cannot decrease \(L_k\) while the region remains fixed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The master minimizes the epigraph of the maximum accumulated convex minorant; its value is a valid regional lower bound and increases monotonically as cuts are added.
assumptions_latex: \(C_k\) is nonempty and convex.
Every \(m_j\) is convex and minorizes \(f\) on \(C_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_k\le\inf_{C_k}f\), and adding valid minorants cannot lower \(L_k\) for fixed \(C_k\).

knowledge_statements.title: Tree-Based Bounding Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic branch-and-bound using DC regional lower bounds and feasible incumbents.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Input a compact initial region \(C_0\), objective \(f=g-h\), and tolerance \(\tau\ge0\). Maintain active nodes \(R\subseteq C_0\), valid bounds \(L(R)\le\inf_{x\in R}f(x)\), and an incumbent value \(B\) from feasible evaluations. Repeatedly select an active node with smallest lower bound. If \(L(R)\ge B-\tau\), prune it; otherwise partition it into finitely many children, compute their valid lower bounds, update \(B\), and retain unpruned children. Stop when
\[
B-\min_{R\text{ active}}L(R)\le\tau,
\]
or no active node remains. Return the incumbent point and \(B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Branch-and-bound partitions the domain, computes valid regional DC lower bounds, prunes regions unable to improve the incumbent, and terminates at the prescribed global gap.
assumptions_latex: \(C_0\) is compact and every generated child family covers its parent.
Each \(L(R)\) is a valid regional lower bound.
Incumbent values arise from feasible points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At termination the returned incumbent satisfies \(f(\bar x)\le\inf_{x\in C_0}f(x)+\tau\).

notation.meaning: lower bound for search region R

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite-Tolerance Convergence Under Uniformly Consistent Refinement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient convergence regime for regional DC branch-and-bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let active regions cover every unresolved feasible point of a compact set \(F\). Suppose that at iteration \(k\) every active region has diameter at most \(\delta_k\), where \(\delta_k\to0\), and that functions \(\omega,\eta\) satisfy \(\omega(t),\eta(t)\to0\) as \(t\downarrow0\). For each active region \(R\), assume \[\inf_{x\in F\cap R}f(x)-\omega(\operatorname{diam}R)\le L(R)\le\inf_{x\in F\cap R}f(x),\] and assume a feasible trial associated with every active region has value at most \(\inf_{F\cap R}f+\eta(\operatorname{diam}R)\). If \(L_k=\min_R L(R)\) and \(U_k\) is the incumbent value, then \[0\le U_k-L_k\le\omega(\delta_k)+\eta(\delta_k).\] Consequently, every positive absolute tolerance is certified after finitely many iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniformly shrinking covered regions, uniformly consistent lower bounds, and uniformly accurate feasible trials force the global branch-and-bound gap to zero and give finite epsilon termination.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is nonempty and compact, and active regions cover all unresolved feasible points.
The maximum active-region diameter \(\delta_k\) tends to zero unless the algorithm terminates.
Regional lower-bound error is bounded by \(\omega(\operatorname{diam}R)\).
Regional feasible-trial error is bounded by \(\eta(\operatorname{diam}R)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: 0\le U_k-L_k\le\omega(\delta_k)+\eta(\delta_k)\to0.

notation.meaning: uniform lower-bound and feasible-trial error moduli

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min\{f(x):x\in F\}\), where \(F\subseteq R_0\), and let \(\varepsilon\ge0\). Maintain active node regions \(R\subseteq R_0\), a feasible incumbent \(\hat x\in F\), and \(U=f(\hat x)\). At a node \(R\), solve an outer relaxation containing \(F\cap R\) and obtain a rigorous lower bound \(L_R\). Use only cuts valid on \(R\), and inherit such a cut at a descendant \(R'\subseteq R\) only when it remains valid there. Update \(\hat x\) and \(U\) whenever a better feasible point is found. Prune \(R\) if its relaxation is infeasible or \(L_R\ge U-\varepsilon\); otherwise replace it by children whose union contains \(F\cap R\). If no active node remains, return \(\hat x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coordinate node relaxations, valid cuts, feasible incumbents, pruning, and coverage-preserving branching. If this process exhausts the active tree, its incumbent has absolute objective gap at most the requested tolerance.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete one-dimensional witnesses for invalid cuts, overstated bounds, and incomplete child coverage.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min\{x:0\le x\le1\}\), whose unique minimizer is \(0\), and suppose the incumbent is \(x=1\) with value \(U=1\). An invalid cut \(x\ge\tfrac12\) removes the minimizer. Alternatively, assigning the region containing \(0\) the invalid lower bound \(\widetilde L=1\) permits it to be pruned against \(U\). Finally, replacing \([0,1]\) only by the child \([\tfrac12,1]\) loses coverage even when every bound on that child is valid. Each alteration permits exhaustion of the represented search while the returned incumbent is not globally optimal.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure boundary specific to interactions among outer-approximation cuts, node bounds, pruning, and branching.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A combined cut–tree method can produce a false certificate if a cut excludes an improving feasible point, a computed node value exceeds the true node infimum, or the children fail to cover the feasible portion of their parent. knowledge_statements.statement_title: Simplicial Interpolation Branch-and-Bound for Separated Nonconvexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simplicial convex lower bounding and convergence when the subtracted convex term depends on a separated variable block.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min\{G(x,y)-H(y):(x,y)\in C,\ y\in Y\}\), where \(C\) is convex, \(Y\) is a compact polytope, and \(G,H\) are convex. For a simplex \(S=\operatorname{conv}\{v_0,\ldots,v_m\}\) in a triangulation of \(Y\), let \(\overline H_S\) be the affine vertex interpolant of \(H\). Then \(H(y)\le\overline H_S(y)\) on \(S\), so minimizing \(G(x,y)-\overline H_S(y)\) over \((x,y)\in C\), \(y\in S\), gives a convex regional lower bound. A simplicial branch-and-bound method subdivides live simplices, updates feasible incumbents, and prunes by rigorous lower bounds. Under fair exhaustive refinement with maximum live-simplex diameter tending to zero, rigorous node solution, and consistent incumbent generation, interpolation error vanishes uniformly and the incumbent–lower-bound gap converges to zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Triangulate the separated variable polytope, use affine vertex overestimators to form convex node bounds, and refine exhaustively to global convergence.
assumptions_latex: \(Y\) is a compact polytope admitting a finite conforming triangulation.
The relevant feasible region is nonempty and compact, and \(C\) is convex.
\(G\) and \(H\) are finite and convex on the relevant domain.
Refinement is fair and exhaustive, node bounds are rigorous, and maximum live-simplex diameter tends to zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every simplicial node supplies a valid convex lower bound, and exhaustive vanishing-mesh refinement yields global bound-gap convergence.

notation.meaning: compact polytope for the separated variables

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Rectangular Secant Branch-and-Bound for Separated Nonconvexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boxwise convex lower bounding and convergence for coordinate-separable subtracted convex terms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(\min\{G(x,y)-\sum_{j=1}^mH_j(y_j):(x,y)\in C,\ y\in Y\}\), where \(C\) is convex, \(Y\) is a compact box, and \(G,H_j\) are convex. On \(R=\prod_j[a_j,b_j]\subseteq Y\), let \(s_{j,R}\) be the endpoint secant of \(H_j\). Then \(H_j(t)\le s_{j,R}(t)\), and minimizing
\[G(x,y)-\sum_j s_{j,R}(y_j)\]
over \((x,y)\in C\), \(y\in R\), gives a convex regional lower-bounding problem. A rectangular branch-and-bound method bisects live boxes, updates feasible incumbents, and safely prunes boxes whose rigorous lower bounds cannot improve the incumbent. If selection and branching are exhaustive, live-box widths tend to zero, node problems are bounded rigorously, and feasible incumbents are generated consistently, the aggregate secant error vanishes uniformly and the usual incumbent–lower-bound test yields global convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coordinatewise secants create convex box lower bounds for a separated subtracted term; exhaustive shrinking-box branch-and-bound converges globally.

\(Y\) is a compact box.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Cellwise Lower Models from Noncanonical DC Decompositions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity, strengthening order, and tractability boundary for lower models induced by a chosen DC decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f(z)=G(z)-H(Az)\) on \(Z_R\), where \(G\) and \(H\) are convex and \(AZ_R\subseteq R\). If \(\overline H_R\) satisfies \(H(y)\le\overline H_R(y)\) on \(R\), then
\[m_R(z)=G(z)-\overline H_R(Az)\le f(z)\quad(z\in Z_R),\]
so any rigorous lower bound on \(\inf_{Z_R}m_R\) is a valid regional lower bound. If two valid overestimators satisfy \(\overline H_R^{(1)}\le\overline H_R^{(0)}\), then \(m_R^{(1)}\ge m_R^{(0)}\). The subproblem is convex when \(\overline H_R\circ A\) is concave, in particular when \(\overline H_R\) is affine; convexity of \(\overline H_R\) alone does not provide this tractability guarantee.

Noncanonical DC Outer Approximation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Outer relaxation based on a chosen, noncanonical DC decomposition over partition cells.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f(z)=G(z)-H(Az)\) on a compact convex set \(Z\), with \(G\) and \(H\) convex. For a cell \(R\) containing \(AZ_R:=\{Az:z\in Z_R\}\), choose a convexly tractable overestimator \(\overline H_R\) satisfying \(H(y)\le\overline H_R(y)\) for every \(y\in R\). Then
\[
L_R:=\inf_{z\in Z_R}\bigl(G(z)-\overline H_R(Az)\bigr)\le \inf_{z\in Z_R}f(z).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-tolerance global level-feasibility search, its stopping certificate, and its finite-success bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\ne\varnothing\), let \(f=g-h\) be bounded below on \(F\), choose \(x^0\in F\), and set \(U_0=f(x^0)\). For fixed \(\varepsilon>0\), at iteration \(k\) globally find an \(x\in F\) satisfying \(f(x)<U_k-\varepsilon\), or certify that none exists. A witness becomes the next incumbent. Infeasibility implies \(U_k\le\inf_F f+\varepsilon\). If \(f_*=\inf_F f\), every successful iteration decreases the incumbent by more than \(\varepsilon\), so the number \(N\) of successful iterations satisfies \(N<(U_0-f_*)/\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly search globally below the incumbent by a fixed margin; a witness improves it, while infeasibility certifies epsilon-global optimality and forces finite termination.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Successive Incumbent-Transcending Level Search
Successive Incumbent-Transcending Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact level-feasibility scheme that repeatedly seeks a point improving the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(f=g-h\) on a compact feasible set \(F\), choose a feasible \(x^0\), set \(U_0=f(x^0)\), and fix \(\varepsilon>0\). At iteration \(k\), globally solve or certify infeasibility of the level problem
\[
\text{find }x\in F\text{ such that }g(x)-h(x)<U_k-\varepsilon.
\]
If infeasible, return \(x^k\); it is \(\varepsilon\)-globally optimal. If a feasible \(x^{k+1}\) is found, set \(U_{k+1}=f(x^{k+1})\) and repeat. With an exact feasibility oracle, every successful iteration decreases the incumbent by more than \(\varepsilon\), so boundedness below implies finitely many successful iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly solve a global level-feasibility problem below the incumbent. A witness improves the incumbent; infeasibility certifies that no point improves it by the prescribed tolerance.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Outer-Safe Treatment of Hard DC Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Containment and penalty conditions needed to preserve hard DC constraints during global bounding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For node \(R\) and constraints \(c_i(x)=g_i(x)-h_i(x)\le0\), suppose \(\underline c_{i,R}(x)\le c_i(x)\) for every \(x\in R\). Then
\[\{x\in R:c_i(x)\le0\ \forall i\}\subseteq\{x\in R:\underline c_{i,R}(x)\le0\ \forall i\}.\]
Certified infeasibility of the relaxed system therefore certifies infeasibility of the original node. Replacing hard constraints by a finite penalty is equivalent only under a problem-specific exact-penalty theorem. Indeed, for any fixed \(\rho<\infty\), minimizing \(- (\rho+1)|x|+\rho|x|\) on \([-1,1]\) as a penalty replacement for the hard constraint \(x=0\) yields minimizers \(x=\pm1\), whereas the constrained feasible set is \(\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hard DC constraints must remain outer-safe in node relaxations; an arbitrary finite penalty is not an exact replacement.
assumptions_latex: Each \(g_i\) and \(h_i\) is convex on the node domain.
Node rejection uses certified infeasibility of a relaxation containing the original feasible set.
Any asserted penalty replacement has an independently justified exact-penalty threshold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Relaxation infeasibility is safe under outer containment, while finite penalization is unsafe without exactness hypotheses.
