\(g:U\to\mathbb R\) is convex.
\(g(\bar x)=0\) and \(0\in\partial g(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{y\in U:g(y)<0\}=\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: convex subdifferential at the active point
strict convex exclusion induced by g

knowledge_statements.title: Zero-Subgradient Redundancy Criterion
Reverse-Convex Boundary Degeneracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic activity with a vanishing gradient need not describe a regular feasible boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_{x\in[-1,1]}x^2\) subject to the reverse-convex inequality \(g(x):=x^2\geq0\). The unique minimizer is \(x^*=0\), where \(g(x^*)=0\) and \(g'(x^*)=0\). Moreover, \(g(x)\geq0\) holds throughout the host, so \(x^*\) is not on the relative topological boundary of the feasible set. The first-order linearization at \(x^*\) is the vacuous inequality \(0\geq0\). Thus algebraic activity alone does not provide a regular reverse-convex boundary or a nonzero supporting normal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reverse-convex constraint can be algebraically active with zero gradient while remaining locally redundant, so its zero level set does not furnish a regular feasible boundary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^*=0\), \(g(x^*)=g'(x^*)=0\), and \(x^*\notin\operatorname{relbd}\{x\in C:g(x)\geq0\}\).

children.title: Nonisolated Reverse-Convex Solutions
children.top_down_role: Solution sets containing continua or locally indistinguishable optima.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Topological classification of global minimizers within a reverse-convex solution set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S^*=\operatorname{argmin}_{x\in F}f(x)\). A point \(x^*\in S^*\) is isolated if some \(\varepsilon>0\) satisfies \(S^*\cap B_\varepsilon(x^*)=\{x^*\}\). It is nonisolated if every \(\varepsilon>0\) satisfies \((S^*\setminus\{x^*\})\cap B_\varepsilon(x^*)\ne\varnothing\). Thus nonisolatedness means accumulation by other global solutions, not merely the existence of several separated minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A global solution is nonisolated exactly when other global solutions occur arbitrarily close to it; separated multiplicity alone is insufficient.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a reverse-convex feasible set.
\(S^*=\operatorname{argmin}_{x\in F}f(x)\ne\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^*\text{ is nonisolated}\iff \forall\varepsilon>0,\ (S^*\setminus\{x^*\})\cap B_\varepsilon(x^*)\ne\varnothing.

notation.meaning: open Euclidean ball about the solution

knowledge_statements.title: Isolated and Nonisolated Global Solutions
Nonisolated Reverse-Convex Solutions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A reverse-convex program can have continua of global minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(C=[-1,1]^2\), minimize \(f(x)=x_2^2\) subject to the convex exclusion inequality \(g(x):=x_1^2-1/4\geq0\). The feasible set is the union of two closed strips. Its global optimal value is \(0\), and the solution set is \[S^*=\bigl([-1,-1/2]\cup[1/2,1]\bigr)\times\{0\}.\] Every point of \(S^*\) is a global minimizer and none is isolated within \(S^*\). Hence finiteness or isolatedness of reverse-convex solutions requires additional assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quadratic objective constant along feasible strips yields two line segments of global minimizers rather than isolated solutions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S^*=([-1,-1/2]\cup[1/2,1])\times\{0\}\) is nonisolated.

children.title: Degenerate Solution Manifolds
children.top_down_role: Nonisolated solution structures supported by degenerate boundaries.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Opposing host and reverse-convex boundaries can support a positive-dimensional, tangentially flat optimal manifold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n\geq2\), \(C=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:\|x\|_2\leq1\}\), impose \(g(x):=\|x\|_2^2-1\geq0\), and minimize \(f(x)=0\). The host inequality and reverse-convex inequality together give \(S^*=\{x:\|x\|_2=1\}\). Thus the feasible and optimal set is an \((n-1)\)-dimensional manifold. The objective is flat in every tangent direction, so optimizer isolation, positive tangential curvature, and finite-candidate conclusions fail.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Opposing ball constraints leave the sphere, and a constant objective makes that entire positive-dimensional manifold globally optimal and tangentially flat.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S^*=\{x:\|x\|_2=1\}\text{ is an }(n-1)\text{-dimensional global-solution manifold}.

children.title: Boundary-Localization Failure
children.top_down_role: Limits of localization mechanisms near degenerate or nonisolated solutions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Without hypotheses excluding flat interior optima, global optimizers need not lie on exclusion boundaries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=[-2,2]\), impose the reverse-convex inequality \(g(x):=x^2-1\geq0\), and minimize \(f(x)=0\). Every feasible point is globally optimal. In particular, \(x=3/2\) is optimal and satisfies \(g(3/2)=5/4>0\), so it is not on the exclusion boundary \(g(x)=0\). Hence a universal claim that every optimizer lies on an active exclusion boundary is false without additional objective hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constant objective makes strictly feasible points optimal, disproving unconditional localization of every optimizer to an exclusion boundary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x=3/2\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C,\ g(x)\geq0}f(x),\qquad g(3/2)>0.
knowledge_statements.title: Boundary-Localization Failure
Unbounded Convex Hosts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dropping compactness can destroy existence and finite lower bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Take the unbounded convex host \(C=\mathbb R\), impose the reverse-convex inequality \(g(x):=x^2-1\geq0\), and minimize \(f(x)=-x\). The feasible set is \(( -\infty,-1]\cup[1,\infty)\). Along the feasible sequence \(x_k=k\), one has \(f(x_k)=-k\to-\infty\). Hence the problem is unbounded below and has no global minimizer. Compact-host existence arguments and algorithms requiring bounded polyhedral enumeration cannot be transferred to unbounded hosts without coercivity, level-boundedness, or explicit valid bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On an unbounded host, a reverse-convex feasible ray can let the objective diverge to minus infinity, so no global minimizer exists.
assumptions_latex: \(C=\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf\{f(x):x\in C,\ g(x)\geq0\}=-\infty\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Level-Boundedness Restores Attainment on an Unbounded Host
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient replacement for compact-host assumptions in reverse-convex minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty and closed, and let \(f:F\to\mathbb R\) be lower semicontinuous. If \(f\) is level-bounded on \(F\), meaning that \(\{x\in F:f(x)\leq\alpha\}\) is bounded for every \(\alpha\in\mathbb R\), then \(f\) attains a finite global minimum on \(F\), even when the convex host containing \(F\) is unbounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Closed feasibility, lower semicontinuity, and level-boundedness restore finite attainment even on an unbounded host.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty and closed.
\(f:F\to\mathbb R\) is lower semicontinuous.
For every \(\alpha\in\mathbb R\), \(\{x\in F:f(x)\leq\alpha\}\) is bounded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{argmin}_{x\in F}f(x)\ne\varnothing\quad\text{and}\quad\min_{x\in F}f(x)\in\mathbb R\).

knowledge_statements.title: Monomial Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-variable monomials used in geometric programming.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A monomial on the positive orthant \(\mathbb R_{++}^n\) is a function \[m(x)=c\prod_{j=1}^n x_j^{a_j},\] where \(c>0\) and the exponents \(a_j\in\mathbb R\) are arbitrary real numbers. Under the logarithmic substitution \(y_j=\log x_j\), its logarithm is affine: \[\log m(e^y)=\log c+a^{\mathsf T}y.\] Consequently, an equality between two monomials becomes an affine equality in logarithmic variables, and a monomial inequality can be normalized and represented by an affine logarithmic inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive coefficient times arbitrary real powers of positive variables is a monomial; taking logarithms converts it to an affine function.
assumptions_latex: \(x\in\mathbb R_{++}^n\).
\(c>0\) and \(a\in\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\log m(e^y)=\log c+a^{\mathsf T}y\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Log-Affinity Does Not Imply Ordinary Convexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between geometric log-space structure and convexity in the original variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A geometric-programming monomial need not be convex in its original positive variables. For example, \(m(x)=x^{1/2}\) on \(\mathbb R_{++}\) satisfies \(\log m(e^y)=y/2\), while \(m''(x)=-1/(4x^{3/2})<0\), so it is strictly concave. Thus monomial log-affinity cannot be replaced by ordinary convexity in \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Monomials are log-affine but need not be convex in their original variables; the square-root monomial is strictly concave.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Log-affinity of a monomial does not imply convexity in the original coordinates.
knowledge_statements.title: Log-Affinity Does Not Imply Ordinary Convexity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closure rules for geometric-programming monomials on the positive orthant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(m_1(x)=c_1x^a\) and \(m_2(x)=c_2x^b\) be monomials on \(\mathbb R_{++}^n\), with \(c_1,c_2>0\), and let \(r\in\mathbb R\). Then
\[m_1m_2=(c_1c_2)x^{a+b},\qquad \frac{m_1}{m_2}=\frac{c_1}{c_2}x^{a-b},\qquad m_1^r=c_1^r x^{ra}\]
are monomials. Consequently every finite product, ratio, or real power of positive monomials remains log-affine after \(y=\log x\). A sum of two nonproportional monomials is generally a posynomial rather than a monomial.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive monomials are closed under products, ratios, and real powers, but generally not under addition.
assumptions_latex: \(x\in\mathbb R_{++}^n\).
\(m_1,m_2\) have positive coefficients.
\(r\in\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Products, ratios, and real powers preserve the monomial class and log-affinity.
knowledge_statements.title: Algebraic Closure of Positive Monomials
Posynomial Geometric Programs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard-form geometric programs and their logarithmic convex reformulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A standard posynomial geometric program minimizes a posynomial \(f_0(x)\) over \(x\in\mathbb R_{++}^n\), subject to \(f_i(x)\leq1\) for posynomials \(f_i\) and \(m_j(x)=1\) for monomials \(m_j\). Write \(x=e^y\). Each transformed inequality is \[\log f_i(e^y)=\log\!\left(\sum_{k=1}^{K_i}\exp(a_{ik}^{\mathsf T}y+b_{ik})\right)\leq0,\] which is convex in \(y\), while each monomial equality becomes affine. Minimizing \(f_0\) is equivalently minimizing \(\log f_0(e^y)\); hence the transformed problem is a convex optimization problem with the same minimizers under \(x=e^y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Logarithmic variables turn posynomial inequalities into log-sum-exp constraints and monomial equalities into affine constraints, yielding an equivalent convex problem.
assumptions_latex: \(x\in\mathbb R_{++}^n\).
All posynomial coefficients are strictly positive.
All monomial equality coefficients are strictly positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x=e^y\) gives an equivalent convex formulation in \(y\).

\(m\) is a monomial and \(\alpha>0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A generalized geometric program in the broad positive-domain sense has the form
\[
\inf_{x\in X}\ F_0(x)\quad\text{subject to}\quad F_j(x)\leq 1\ (j=1,\ldots,m),
\]
where \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}_{++}^n\), and every \(F_j\) is constructed from finitely many monomials \(c\prod_{i=1}^n x_i^{a_i}\), with \(c\in\mathbb{R}\) and \(a_i\in\mathbb{R}\), by finite addition and, where specified, ratios whose denominators remain positive on \(X\). Negative coefficients or nonmonomial denominators generally destroy the standard geometric-program convexification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A generalized geometric program optimizes finite positive-domain expressions assembled from real-power monomials, possibly with signed sums or positive ratios; such extensions are generally nonconvex after logarithmic transformation.
knowledge_statements.title: Generalized Geometric Programs

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Generalized geometric programs and the posynomial-only restriction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines monomials, posynomials, and difference-of-posynomial generalized geometric programs. The extract inconsistently combines arbitrary real exponents and positive variables with displayed nonnegative variable bounds, and its printed posynomial constraints are infeasible on a strictly positive domain when their coefficients are positive.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A monomial is \(g_k(t)=\prod_{i=1}^N t_i^{\alpha_{ijk}}\), and a posynomial is \(G_j^{\pm}(t)=\sum_{k\in K_j^{\pm}}c_{jk}\prod_{i=1}^N t_i^{\alpha_{ijk}}\), where \(c_{jk}>0\) and \(\alpha_{ijk}\in\mathbb R\). A generalized geometric program has the difference-of-posynomials form \[\min_t\;G_0^+(t)-G_0^-(t)\quad\text{s.t.}\quad G_j^+(t)-G_j^-(t)\le 0,\quad j=1,\ldots,M,\] on the common domain of its power products. Setting \(K_j^-=\varnothing\) for every \(j=0,\ldots,M\) gives the formal posynomial-only restriction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A monomial is a product of variables raised to arbitrary real powers, and a posynomial is a finite positive linear combination of monomials. A generalized geometric program minimizes a difference of posynomials subject to difference-of-posynomial inequalities. Removing all negatively signed monomials gives the formal posynomial-only restriction. Arbitrary real powers generally require strictly positive variables; moreover, the extract's printed positive-posynomial constraints G_j^+ ≤ 0 have no solution on that domain unless a degenerate convention is introduced.
assumptions_latex: \(K_j^+\) and \(K_j^-\) are finite for \(j=0,\ldots,M\).
\(c_{jk}>0\) and \(\alpha_{ijk}\in\mathbb R\).
\(t\) belongs to the common domain of every power product; ordinarily \(t\in\mathbb R_{++}^N\) when arbitrary real exponents occur.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The functions \(G_j=G_j^+-G_j^-\) define the generalized geometric-program family, while \(K_j^-=\varnothing\) for all \(j\) gives its formal posynomial-only restriction.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A complementary geometric program is a problem representable as
\[
\inf_{x\in X}\ \frac{p_0(x)}{q_0(x)}\quad\text{subject to}\quad \frac{p_j(x)}{q_j(x)}\leq 1\quad(j=1,\ldots,m),
\]
where \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}_{++}^n\) and each \(p_j,q_j\) is a posynomial, with \(q_j(x)>0\) on \(X\). Constraints with denominator \(1\) and a posynomial objective are included. Unlike an ordinary geometric program, the log-domain expression \(\log p_j(\exp y)-\log q_j(\exp y)\) is generally a difference of convex functions rather than a convex function.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A complementary geometric program has posynomial ratios in its objective or constraints. Positive denominators make the ratios well-defined, but their logarithms are generally differences of convex functions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact embedding of complementary constraints and ratio objectives into a signomial model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p,q\) be posynomials and \(q(x)>0\) on \(X\subseteq\mathbb R_{++}^n\). Then \(p(x)/q(x)\le1\) is equivalent to \(p(x)-q(x)\le0\). Likewise, minimizing \(p_0/q_0\) is equivalent in infimum value to minimizing \(t>0\) subject to \(p_0(x)-tq_0(x)\le0\); the latter is a signomial inequality in \((x,t)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive denominators can be cleared exactly, embedding complementary constraints and epigraphed ratio objectives into general signomial programs.

\(p,q,p_0,q_0\) are posynomials.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A general signomial program has the form
\[
\inf_{x\in X}\ s_0(x)\quad\text{subject to}\quad s_j(x)\leq 0\ (j=1,\ldots,m),
\]
where \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}_{++}^n\) and
\[
s_j(x)=\sum_{k=1}^{K_j}c_{jk}\prod_{i=1}^n x_i^{a_{ijk}},
\]
with \(K_j<\infty\), coefficients \(c_{jk}\in\mathbb{R}\), and exponents \(a_{ijk}\in\mathbb{R}\). Zero coefficients may be omitted. Because coefficients of either sign are allowed, neither \(s_j\) nor its logarithmic-coordinate form is required to be convex, and the formulation includes ordinary geometric programs as a restricted subclass.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A general signomial program optimizes finite sums of real-power monomials over positive variables, allowing arbitrary real coefficients and therefore potentially nonconvex objectives and constraints.

Splitting positive and negative coefficients yields \(s(\exp y)=P(y)-N(y)\), where \(P\) and \(N\) are finite nonnegative sums of exponentials and hence convex.

knowledge_statements.title: Exponential-Sum and Difference-of-Convex Representation
Positive-Domain Multiplicative Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic representation of positive power-product atoms, signed generalized monomial terms, and finite signomials on the strictly positive orthant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(x\in\mathbb{R}_{++}^n\) and \(a\in\mathbb{R}^n\), define the positive multiplicative atom
\[
\phi_a(x)=\prod_{i=1}^n x_i^{a_i}.
\]
A signed generalized monomial term has the representation \(m_{c,a}(x)=c\phi_a(x)\), where \(c\in\mathbb{R}\). The atom \(\phi_a(x)\) is strictly positive and well-defined for arbitrary real exponents, whereas the sign of \(m_{c,a}(x)\) is determined by \(c\). Every finite signomial can consequently be represented as
\[
s(x)=\sum_{k=1}^K m_{c_k,a_k}(x)=\sum_{k=1}^K c_k\prod_{i=1}^n x_i^{a_{ik}}.
\]
The restriction \(x\in\mathbb{R}_{++}^n\) is essential when noninteger real exponents are allowed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On the positive orthant, a real exponent vector defines a strictly positive power-product atom. A generalized monomial term is a real coefficient times that atom, and a finite signomial is a sum of such signed terms.
assumptions_latex: \(x_i>0\) for every \(i=1,\ldots,n\).
The exponent vector belongs to \(\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every finite signomial is a real linear combination of the strictly positive multiplicative atoms \(\phi_a(x)=\prod_i x_i^{a_i}\).

Thus positive power-product atoms are closed under multiplication, division, and real powers.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 8. Generalized Geometric Programming: Theory p. 257

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(y_i=\log x_i\), equivalently \(x_i=\exp(y_i)\). For every exponent vector \(a_k\in\mathbb{R}^n\),
\[
\prod_{i=1}^n x_i^{a_{ik}}=\exp\!\left(\sum_{i=1}^n a_{ik}y_i\right)=\exp(a_k^{\mathsf T}y).
\]
Hence the finite signomial \(s(x)=\sum_{k=1}^K c_k\prod_i x_i^{a_{ik}}\) has the exact log-domain exponential representation
\[
s(\exp y)=\sum_{k=1}^K c_k\exp(a_k^{\mathsf T}y).
\]
This change of variables is a bijection between \(\mathbb{R}_{++}^n\) and \(\mathbb{R}^n\), so it preserves feasible points and objective values under consistent substitution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Taking componentwise logarithms bijectively maps positive variables to unrestricted coordinates, converts each monomial into an exponential of a linear form, and converts each signomial into a signed exponential sum.
knowledge_statements.title: Log-Domain Exponential Representation

notation.meaning: Convex positive and negative exponential sums.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical coefficient-sign split of a finite log-domain signomial into two convex exponential sums.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 8. Generalized Geometric Programming: Theory p. 257

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Partition the nonzero coefficients using \(P=\{k:c_k>0\}\) and \(N=\{k:c_k<0\}\), and define
\[
g(y)=\sum_{k\in P}c_k\exp(a_k^{\mathsf T}y),\qquad h(y)=\sum_{k\in N}(-c_k)\exp(a_k^{\mathsf T}y).
\]
Each summand is a positive multiple of an exponential of an affine function, so \(g\) and \(h\) are convex on \(\mathbb{R}^n\). The signomial therefore satisfies the exact difference-of-convex identity
\[
s(\exp y)=g(y)-h(y).
\]
Empty sums are interpreted as zero. This representation establishes DC structure but does not by itself make constraints of the form \(g(y)-h(y)\leq 0\) convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Splitting a log-domain signomial into its positive- and negative-coefficient exponential sums writes it exactly as one convex function minus another, without eliminating its nonconvexity.
knowledge_statements.title: Signomial-to-DC Representation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact ratio representation obtained by separating a signomial into positive and negative posynomial parts.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 8. Generalized Geometric Programming: Theory p. 257

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given a finite signomial \(s(x)=\sum_k c_kx^{a_k}\), define its positive and negative parts by
\[
p(x)=\sum_{c_k>0}c_kx^{a_k},\qquad q(x)=\sum_{c_k<0}(-c_k)x^{a_k}.
\]
Then \(s(x)=p(x)-q(x)\), with \(p\) and \(q\) posynomials. Whenever \(q(x)>0\), the constraint has the exact ratio-based representation
\[
s(x)\leq 0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad p(x)\leq q(x)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \frac{p(x)}{q(x)}\leq 1.
\]
If \(q\) is identically zero or can vanish on an enlarged domain, the ratio form is unavailable there although the difference form remains meaningful.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Separating positive and negative terms writes a signomial inequality as one posynomial bounded by another, or equivalently as a posynomial ratio bounded by one when the denominator is positive.

assumptions_latex: \(p(x)>0\) and \(q(x)>0\) on \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}_{++}^n\).
The auxiliary variable is restricted to \(t>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The ratio constraint \(p(x)/q(x)\leq 1\) is exactly the projection onto \(x\) of \(p(x)\leq t\leq q(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-variable exact lift of a positive ratio inequality through an intermediate positive bound.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 8. Generalized Geometric Programming: Theory p. 257

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For positive functions \(p,q:X\to\mathbb{R}_{++}\), define the lifted set
\[
L=\{(x,t):x\in X,\ t>0,\ p(x)\leq t,\ t\leq q(x)\}.
\]
Its projection onto the original variables is exactly
\[
\operatorname{proj}_x L=\left\{x\in X:\frac{p(x)}{q(x)}\leq 1\right\}.
\]
Indeed, feasibility of \(t\) is equivalent to the interval \([p(x),q(x)]\) being nonempty. Multiple ratio constraints may be lifted with separate variables \(t_j\). The lift preserves the original feasible set under projection, although subsequent relaxations of its two linking inequalities need not match a direct relaxation of the ratio.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive ratio constraint is exactly lifted by inserting a positive variable between its numerator and denominator; projecting away that variable recovers the original constraint.
knowledge_statements.title: Auxiliary-Variable Signomial Representations

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 8. Generalized Geometric Programming: Theory p. 257

children.title: Ratio-Lifting Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Connections between ratio structures and lifted auxiliary-variable forms.

knowledge_statements.title: Ratio-Lifting Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact algebraic interfaces connecting signomial differences, strictly positive ratios, auxiliary lifts, and logarithmic coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each split signomial constraint with \(p_j(x)>0\) and \(q_j(x)>0\), the exact interfaces are
\[
p_j(x)-q_j(x)\leq 0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\frac{p_j(x)}{q_j(x)}\leq 1
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\exists t_j>0:\ p_j(x)\leq t_j\leq q_j(x).
\]
Under \(x=\exp y\), the ratio interface also satisfies
\[
\frac{p_j(\exp y)}{q_j(\exp y)}\leq 1
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\log p_j(\exp y)-\log q_j(\exp y)\leq 0.
\]
These equivalences hold at every point where both \(p_j\) and \(q_j\) are strictly positive. They provide consistent interfaces between multiplicative, ratio, lifted, and log-domain models; replacing an exact relation by a relaxation may break equivalence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When both posynomial parts are strictly positive, a split signomial constraint has equivalent difference, ratio, auxiliary-variable, and logarithmic-difference formulations. Relaxing an interface may destroy equivalence.
assumptions_latex: \(x\in X\subseteq\mathbb{R}_{++}^n\), \(t_j>0\), and \(y=\log x\).
For every \(j\), both \(p_j(x)\) and \(q_j(x)\) are strictly positive on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The difference, ratio, auxiliary-variable, and log-domain interfaces describe the same original feasible points when their positivity conditions and linking relations are imposed exactly.

notation.meaning: Strictly positive posynomial parts of constraint j.
Auxiliary linking variable for constraint j.

children.title: Extended-Formulation Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Structural tradeoffs in size, tightness, and domain requirements of lifted forms.

assumptions_latex: An extended formulation \(L\subseteq X\times T\) satisfies \(F=\operatorname{proj}_x L\).
Relaxations \(R_L\supseteq L\) and \(R_F\supseteq F\) are formed over a prescribed bounded domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact lifting preserves \(F\), but generally \(\operatorname{proj}_x R_L\neq R_F\); formulation size and projected relaxation strength must therefore be assessed separately.

notation.meaning: Relaxations of the lifted and original formulations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projection equivalence versus relaxation strength and model size in exact signomial extended formulations.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 8. Generalized Geometric Programming: Theory p. 257
1.2 Structure of Global Optimization Models p. 3

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F\subseteq X\) be an original signomial feasible set and let \(L\subseteq X\times T\) be an exact lifted formulation satisfying \(F=\operatorname{proj}_x L\). Introducing auxiliary variables can replace composite ratio relations by simpler linking relations, increasing the numbers of variables and constraints. If \(R_L\supseteq L\) and \(R_F\supseteq F\) are relaxations constructed from the lifted and original descriptions, respectively, exact projection equivalence alone does not imply
\[
\operatorname{proj}_x R_L=R_F.
\]
Thus an extended formulation trades model size and additional linking constraints against potentially different projected relaxation strength; neither dominance nor equality follows without specifying the relaxation operators and variable bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact lift preserves feasible points after projection, but its relaxation may be stronger or weaker than a direct relaxation while using additional variables and linking constraints.
knowledge_statements.title: Extended-Formulation Tradeoffs

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 8. Generalized Geometric Programming: Theory p. 257

knowledge_statements.title: Exactly Log-Convexifiable Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard geometric-program regime with a posynomial objective and inequalities, monomial equalities, and strictly positive variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider
\[
\inf_{x\in\mathbb{R}_{++}^n} p_0(x)
\quad\text{subject to}\quad
p_j(x)\leq 1\ \ (j=1,\ldots,m),
\qquad
m_\ell(x)=1\ \ (\ell=1,\ldots,r),
\]
where every \(p_j\), including \(p_0\), is a posynomial and every \(m_\ell\) is a positive monomial. With \(x=\exp y\), an exactly equivalent formulation is
\[
\inf_{y\in\mathbb{R}^n}\log p_0(\exp y)
\quad\text{subject to}\quad
\log p_j(\exp y)\leq 0\ \ (j=1,\ldots,m),
\qquad
\log m_\ell(\exp y)=0\ \ (\ell=1,\ldots,r).
\]
Each log-posynomial expression is a log-sum-exp of affine functions and hence convex, while each log-monomial expression is affine. This is the standard exactly log-convexifiable regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A posynomial objective and posynomial inequalities with monomial equalities become an exactly equivalent convex problem after positive variables and positive model functions are logarithmically transformed.
assumptions_latex: \(x\in\mathbb{R}_{++}^n\).
The objective and every inequality function are posynomials, and every equality function is a positive monomial.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The substitution \(y=\log x\), followed by logarithms of the positive model functions, yields an exactly equivalent convex optimization problem.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 8. Generalized Geometric Programming: Theory p. 257

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 8. Generalized Geometric Programming: Theory p. 257

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Why standard exact log convexification permits monomial equalities but not arbitrary posynomial equalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a positive monomial m, m(x)=1 becomes the affine equality \log m(\exp y)=0. A general posynomial equality p(x)=1 instead becomes \log p(\exp y)=0, which is not generally a convex constraint. For example, x_1+x_2=1 with x_1,x_2>0 becomes e^{y_1}+e^{y_2}=1. The feasible points (\log(1/4),\log(3/4)) and (\log(3/4),\log(1/4)) have an infeasible midpoint because its exponential sum is \sqrt{3}/2<1.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Monomial equalities become affine after logarithms, whereas general posynomial equalities can have nonconvex log-domain level sets.
assumptions_latex: Variables are strictly positive.
The equality right-hand side is normalized to one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The standard geometric-program log convexification does not generally extend from monomial equalities to arbitrary posynomial equalities.
knowledge_statements.title: Posynomial Equality Boundary
Mixed-Sign Nonconvex Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete failure of log-domain convexity caused by a mixed-sign signomial inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The mixed-sign constraint
\[
s(x)=x_1+x_2-x_1x_2-1\leq 0,
\qquad x_1,x_2>0,
\]
is equivalent to \((x_1-1)(x_2-1)\geq 0\). Under \(x_i=\exp(y_i)\), its feasible set is
\[
\{y\in\mathbb{R}^2:y_1\geq 0,\ y_2\geq 0\}
\cup
\{y\in\mathbb{R}^2:y_1\leq 0,\ y_2\leq 0\}.
\]
This set is not convex: \((2,0.1)\) and \((-0.1,-2)\) are feasible, whereas their midpoint \((0.95,-0.95)\) is infeasible. Thus mixed coefficient signs can cross the standard geometric-program convexifiability boundary, although particular mixed-sign instances may still have convex feasible sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mixed signs can destroy logarithmic convexity: this two-variable signomial constraint yields the union of two opposite closed orthants in log coordinates, which is nonconvex.
assumptions_latex: The displayed signomial constraint contains both positive- and negative-coefficient monomials.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Mixed coefficient signs can produce a nonconvex log-domain feasible set, so ordinary geometric-program convexification is not valid in general.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 8. Generalized Geometric Programming: Theory p. 257

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 8. Generalized Geometric Programming: Theory p. 257

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Mixed Signs Are Not Sufficient for Nonconvexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of the converse to the mixed-sign nonconvexity warning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The mixed-sign inequality x-1\leq0 with x>0 becomes e^y-1\leq0 under x=e^y, and its feasible set is the convex half-line \{y:y\leq0\}. Thus mixed coefficient signs do not by themselves imply a nonconvex log-domain feasible set; they remove the general convexity guarantee furnished by the geometric-program sign pattern.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mixed-sign signomial can still have a convex log-domain feasible set, so mixed signs remove a guarantee rather than provide a complete nonconvexity test.
assumptions_latex: y=\log x.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Mixed coefficient signs are not sufficient for log-domain nonconvexity.
knowledge_statements.title: Mixed Signs Are Not Sufficient for Nonconvexity

knowledge_statements.statement_title: NP-Hardness on a Compact Positive Box
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case hardness of unrestricted mixed-sign signomial optimization even with integer exponents and bounded positive variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Weighted MAX-CUT is represented by maximizing the multilinear quadratic C(z)=\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E}w_{ij}(z_i+z_j-2z_iz_j) over z\in[0,1]^{|V|}; an optimum occurs at z\in\{0,1\}^{|V|}. Under x=\mathbf 1+z, minimizing -C(x-\mathbf 1) over x\in[1,2]^{|V|} is an unrestricted mixed-sign signomial problem with integer exponents and the same optimal value up to sign. Consequently, global optimization of unrestricted signomials on compact positive boxes is NP-hard.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unrestricted signomial optimization is NP-hard even for mixed-sign quadratic polynomials on the compact positive box [1,2]^n, by a weighted MAX-CUT reduction.
assumptions_latex: Edge weights w_{ij} are nonnegative rational numbers encoded in binary.
The signomial family permits arbitrary real coefficients and nonnegative integer exponents.
The domain is the compact positive box [1,2]^{|V|}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Global minimization of unrestricted mixed-sign signomials on compact positive boxes is NP-hard.

notation.meaning: translation from the unit box to a strictly positive box

knowledge_statements.title: NP-Hardness on a Compact Positive Box

assumptions_latex: The feasible region is a compact positive box \(X=[\ell,u]\subset\mathbb{R}_{++}^n\).
A signomial has the form \(f(x)=\sum_{k=1}^m c_k\prod_{i=1}^n x_i^{a_{ik}}\), with real coefficients and exponents.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Without sign restrictions ensuring convexity after logarithmic transformation, global signomial optimization contains general nonconvex polynomial optimization on positive boxes and admits no general convex reformulation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary for unrestricted mixed-sign signomials on compact positive boxes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the bijection \(y_i=\log x_i\), the signomial becomes \(F(y)=\sum_{k=1}^m c_k e^{a_k^{\mathsf T}y}\). If coefficients of terms appearing on a convex-inequality side have the geometric-programming sign pattern, the transformed formulation can be convex. With unrestricted mixed signs, terms \(c_k e^{a_k^{\mathsf T}y}\) may be concave, and their sums may have multiple local minima. Moreover, ordinary polynomials restricted to \(X\subset\mathbb{R}_{++}^n\) are signomials with nonnegative integer exponents. Hence the unrestricted family contains general box-constrained nonconvex polynomial optimization, so exact log-convexifiability and polynomial-time convex solution cannot be asserted for the family as a whole.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unrestricted mixed-sign signomials include general nonconvex polynomial problems, so logarithmic substitution does not generally yield a convex or tractable global problem.
knowledge_statements.title: General Signomial Hardness Boundary

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role and mathematical direction are plausible, but the record supplies no citation for the claimed containment of general nonconvex polynomial optimization or the resulting tractability boundary. A specific hardness or signomial-complexity source is required.

children.title: Classical Global Relaxations for Signomial Programs
children.top_down_role: Classical family-specific convex relaxations are developed here; modern relative-entropy and positivity hierarchies remain external cross-links.

assumptions_latex: The logarithmic image of the positive domain is a box \(B=[L,U]\subset\mathbb{R}^n\).
Each constraint and the objective are finite sums of exponential-affine terms on \(B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Replacing every nonconvex term by a convex underestimator produces a convex program whose feasible set contains the original feasible set and whose optimum is a valid node lower bound.

notation.meaning: convex underestimator of a transformed signomial

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Termwise convex relaxation after the logarithmic change of variables.

source_refs.locator: 1.4 Deterministic Global Optimization: Approaches and Classes of Problems p. 18

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(\min\{F_0(y):F_j(y)\leq0,\ j=1,\ldots,p,\ y\in B\}\). For every \(j\), construct a convex function \(\underline F_j^B\) satisfying \(\underline F_j^B(y)\leq F_j(y)\) for all \(y\in B\). The boxwise convex relaxation is
\[\beta(B)=\min_{y\in B}\{\underline F_0^B(y):\underline F_j^B(y)\leq0,\ j=1,\ldots,p\}.\]
Every feasible point of the original node problem is feasible for this relaxation, and its relaxed objective does not exceed its original objective. Consequently \(\beta(B)\leq v(B)\), where \(v(B)\) is the original node optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On each log-space box, termwise convex underestimators define a convex relaxation whose optimum is a valid lower bound for the original node problem.
knowledge_statements.title: Boxwise Signomial Convex Relaxations

source_witnesses.locator: 1.4 Deterministic Global Optimization: Approaches and Classes of Problems p. 18

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quadratic Vanishing of Boxwise Term Errors
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform consistency rate for the classical exponential-term relaxation as affine-argument intervals contract.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Write \(F(y)=\sum_{k=1}^m c_k e^{a_k^{\mathsf T}y}\), and let \([\lambda_k(B),\mu_k(B)]\) be the range of \(a_k^{\mathsf T}y\) on \(B\). For the classical termwise underestimator \(\underline F^B\),
\[0\leq F(y)-\underline F^B(y)\leq\frac18\sum_{k:c_k<0}|c_k|e^{\mu_k(B)}\bigl(\mu_k(B)-\lambda_k(B)\bigr)^2\quad(y\in B).\]
Thus the relaxation error converges uniformly to zero whenever all affine-argument widths converge to zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The classical boxwise signomial underestimator has an error bounded quadratically in the affine-argument widths and becomes exact as those widths vanish.
assumptions_latex: \(B\) is a bounded log-space box.
\(F\) is a finite exponential sum.
Each negative-coefficient exponential term is underestimated by its endpoint chord.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_{y\in B}(F(y)-\underline F^B(y))=O(\max_k(\mu_k(B)-\lambda_k(B))^2)\) on bounded families of boxes.

notation.meaning: range of the kth affine exponent on the box

knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic Vanishing of Boxwise Term Errors

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotonic strengthening of classical termwise signomial relaxations under box restriction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B'\subseteq B\) be bounded log-space boxes. Construct each relaxation using exact positive-coefficient exponential terms and endpoint-chord underestimators for negative-coefficient terms. Then, on \(B'\), \(\underline F_j^{B'}(y)\geq\underline F_j^B(y)\) for every relaxed objective or constraint function \(F_j\). Consequently the feasible set of the \(B'\)-relaxation is contained in the restriction to \(B'\) of the \(B\)-relaxation and, whenever their optimal values are defined, \(\beta(B')\geq\beta(B)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recomputing the classical termwise relaxation on a smaller box strengthens its underestimators and cannot decrease the node lower bound.
assumptions_latex: \(B'\subseteq B\) are bounded log-space boxes.
The same exponential-sum formulation is used on both boxes.
Negative-coefficient exponential terms use endpoint-chord underestimators.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\underline F_j^{B'}\geq\underline F_j^B\) on \(B'\) and \(\beta(B')\geq\beta(B)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Nested-Box Relaxation Dominance

assumptions_latex: The scalar argument satisfies \(t=a^{\mathsf T}y\in[\lambda,\mu]\), where \(\lambda<\mu\).
The coefficient satisfies \(c\in\mathbb{R}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The function \(\underline q\) is convex and satisfies \(\underline q(t)\leq c e^t\) for every \(t\in[\lambda,\mu]\); when \(c<0\), equality holds at \(t=\lambda\) and \(t=\mu\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-or-secant convex underestimator on a nondegenerate bounded affine-argument interval.

source_refs.locator: 1.4 Deterministic Global Optimization: Approaches and Classes of Problems p. 18

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(q(t)=c e^t\) on \([\lambda,\mu]\), define
\[\underline q(t)=\begin{cases}c e^t,&c\geq0,\\c\left(\dfrac{\mu-t}{\mu-\lambda}e^{\lambda}+\dfrac{t-\lambda}{\mu-\lambda}e^{\mu}\right),&c<0.\end{cases}\]
This \(\underline q\) is a convex underestimator of \(q\) on \([\lambda,\mu]\). For \(c<0\), it is affine and agrees with \(q\) at both endpoints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative exponential term is retained exactly. A negative exponential term is underestimated by its endpoint secant multiplied by the negative coefficient.
knowledge_statements.title: Exponential-Term Underestimators

source_witnesses.locator: 1.4 Deterministic Global Optimization: Approaches and Classes of Problems p. 18

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform interpolation-error bound for a negative exponential term.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(q(t)=ce^t\) with \(c<0\) on \([\lambda,\mu]\), let \(\underline q\) be its affine endpoint-chord underestimator. Then
\[0\leq q(t)-\underline q(t)\leq\frac{|c|e^\mu}{8}(\mu-\lambda)^2\qquad(\lambda\leq t\leq\mu).\]
Hence \(\underline q\to q\) uniformly at quadratic order as \(\mu-\lambda\to0\) while the intervals remain bounded above.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The negative-exponential chord error is at most one eighth of the maximum curvature magnitude times the squared interval width.
assumptions_latex: \(\lambda<\mu\).
\(\underline q\) is the endpoint chord of \(q(t)=ce^t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|q-\underline q\|_{\infty,[\lambda,\mu]}\leq |c|e^\mu(\mu-\lambda)^2/8\).
knowledge_statements.title: Chord Underestimation Error Bound

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convex-Envelope Exactness of the Negative Exponential Chord
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact convex envelope of a negative exponential on a compact scalar interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(q(t)=ce^t\) on \([\lambda,\mu]\), where \(c<0\) and \(\lambda<\mu\). Its convex envelope is the endpoint chord
\[\operatorname{vex}_{[\lambda,\mu]}q(t)=c\left(\frac{\mu-t}{\mu-\lambda}e^\lambda+\frac{t-\lambda}{\mu-\lambda}e^\mu\right).\]
Equivalently, every convex function \(g\) satisfying \(g\leq q\) on the interval also satisfies \(g\leq\operatorname{vex}_{[\lambda,\mu]}q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a negative exponential term, the endpoint chord is its exact convex envelope on the bounded interval.
assumptions_latex: \(\lambda<\mu\).
\(q(t)=ce^t\) on \([\lambda,\mu]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{vex}_{[\lambda,\mu]}q\) equals the affine endpoint chord.

notation.meaning: convex envelope of q on the interval

knowledge_statements.title: Convex-Envelope Exactness of the Negative Exponential Chord

assumptions_latex: A nonempty finite collection \(\mathcal C\) of node boxes covers the original feasible region.
For every \(B\in\mathcal C\), the relaxation value \(\beta(B)\) is a valid lower bound on the original node optimum \(v(B)\).
A feasible incumbent has value \(U<+\infty\), and \(\varepsilon\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The value \(L=\min_{B\in\mathcal C}\beta(B)\) satisfies \(L\leq v^\star\leq U\), so \(U-L\) is a valid absolute optimality-gap certificate. A node satisfying \(\beta(B)\geq U-\varepsilon\) cannot improve the incumbent by more than \(\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: relaxation optimum on node box B
original optimum on node box B
global lower bound from a covering node collection

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Node lower-bound and global optimality-gap certificates for minimization.

source_refs.locator: 3.6 Finite epsilon-Convergence and epsilon-Global Optimality p. 87

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(v^\star\) be the global optimum of the original minimization problem. For every \(B\in\mathcal C\), validity of the node relaxation gives \(\beta(B)\leq v(B)\). If \(\mathcal C\) covers the original feasible region, then
\[L=\min_{B\in\mathcal C}\beta(B)\leq v^\star\leq U.\]
Hence \(U-L\) is a valid absolute optimality gap. A node satisfying \(\beta(B)\geq U-\varepsilon\) cannot contain a feasible point whose objective is less than \(U-\varepsilon\). An infeasible relaxation certifies infeasibility of the original problem on \(B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lower bounds from a collection of nodes covering the feasible region combine with a feasible incumbent to certify a global gap and safe tolerance-based pruning.
knowledge_statements.title: Signomial Relaxation-Bound Certificates

children.title: Global Search for Generalized Geometric Programs

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Rectangle branch-and-bound algorithm for generalized geometric programs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global-search procedure in transformed variables using convex relaxations, longest-side bisection, feasibility-based incumbent updates, fathoming, and a lower–upper objective gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given tolerances \(\epsilon_f,\epsilon_c>0\), a bounded rectangle \([z^L,z^U]\), valid convex relaxations \(G_j^{\mathrm{conv}}\), and initial bounds \(G_0^{LBD}\le G_0^*\le G_0^{UBD}\), repeatedly: (i) update \(G_0^{UBD}\) at any point satisfying \(\max_jG_j(z)\le\epsilon_f\); (ii) bisect the current rectangle along \(\ell\in\arg\max_i(z_i^U-z_i^L)\); (iii) construct convex relaxations on both children; (iv) fathom a child if its objective lower bound is at least \(G_0^{UBD}\), or if a constraint lower bound is at least zero; (v) solve each surviving relaxation and select the smallest stored relaxation value as \(G_0^{LBD}\) and its rectangle as the next current rectangle. Continue while \(G_0^{UBD}-G_0^{LBD}>\epsilon_c\), and otherwise return the incumbent attaining \(G_0^{UBD}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Initialize a bounded transformed-variable rectangle, feasibility and convergence tolerances, and global objective bounds. At each iteration, use an approximately feasible current point to improve the upper bound, split the current rectangle along its longest side, build and solve convex relaxations on the two children, discard children whose objective or constraint lower bounds prove them noncompetitive or infeasible, and select the stored child having the smallest relaxation value. Stop when the upper–lower objective gap is at most the convergence tolerance and return the best feasible incumbent.
assumptions_latex: \(\epsilon_f>0\) and \(\epsilon_c>0\).
The transformed variables have finite global bounds \(z^L\le z\le z^U\).
Each regional convex relaxation supplies valid objective and constraint lower bounds on its rectangle.
\(G_0^{UBD}\) is generated by an \(\epsilon_f\)-feasible incumbent, and the stored relaxation values are valid lower bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Upon satisfying \(G_0^{UBD}-G_0^{LBD}\le\epsilon_c\), the returned incumbent has an objective value certified within \(\epsilon_c\) of the global lower bound, subject to the stated relaxation-validity and feasibility tolerances.

Each selected box can be split into finitely many boxes whose union equals it.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(\mathcal A_0=\{B^0\}\). At iteration \(k\), select \(B_k\in\mathcal A_k\), choose a coordinate \(i\) and split value \(s\in(L_i,U_i)\), and form the children obtained by replacing \([L_i,U_i]\) with \([L_i,s]\) and \([s,U_i]\). Compute valid relaxations on the children and remove children certified infeasible or unable to improve the incumbent. Set \(\mathcal A_{k+1}\) equal to the surviving children together with the unselected active boxes. Stop when \(\mathcal A_{k+1}=\varnothing\) or the certified global gap meets the prescribed tolerance; return the incumbent and its bound certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partition the positive domain in log coordinates, solve child relaxations, prune certified nodes, and stop when no nodes remain or the certified gap is small.
knowledge_statements.title: Transformed-Space Partitioning

source_witnesses.locator: 2.1.2 Partition Algorithms: A General Scheme p. 46

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric interpretation of rectangular partitioning after logarithmic transformation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the bijection \(y_i=\log x_i\), a log-space box \(B=[L,U]\) corresponds exactly to \(X_B=\prod_{i=1}^n[e^{L_i},e^{U_i}]\). Splitting \(y_i\) at \(s\in(L_i,U_i)\) is equivalent to splitting \(x_i\) at \(e^s\). In particular, log-midpoint bisection uses the geometric-mean split \(e^s=\sqrt{e^{L_i}e^{U_i}}\), and the exponential map preserves exact coverage and interior disjointness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Log-space boxes are multiplicative boxes in positive variables, and a log midpoint is a geometric-mean split.
assumptions_latex: Every original variable is strictly positive.
\(y_i=\log x_i\) and \(B=[L,U]\) has finite endpoints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Log-space splitting is bijectively equivalent to multiplicative original-space box splitting and preserves coverage.
knowledge_statements.title: Log-Box and Multiplicative-Box Equivalence

children.title: Signomial Branching Regimes
children.top_down_role: Branching choices for signomial search in original or transformed spaces.

assumptions_latex: Every active node is a nondegenerate log-space box \(B=[L,U]\).
Branching uses an interior split point and preserves the union of the parent box.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A branching regime is exhaustive when every infinite nested sequence of generated boxes has diameter converging to zero; longest-edge bisection is one such regime.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exhaustive coordinate branching for transformed signomial boxes.

source_refs.locator: 2.4.2 Convergence of Multivariate Rectangular Partition Methods p. 97

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A signomial branching regime selects a coordinate \(i\) and an interior point \(s\in(L_i,U_i)\), replacing \(B=[L,U]\) by two boxes whose union is \(B\) and whose interiors are disjoint. The regime is exhaustive if, for every infinite nested chain \(B^0\supset B^1\supset\cdots\) generated by repeated branching, \(\operatorname{diam}(B^k)\to0\). Longest-edge bisection, which chooses \(i\in\operatorname*{argmax}_j w_j(B)\) and \(s=(L_i+U_i)/2\), satisfies this condition. Branching may instead target the affine-argument interval producing the largest relaxation error, provided exhaustiveness is retained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid regime partitions boxes exactly and is exhaustive: every infinite nested branch shrinks to a point. Longest-edge bisection satisfies this condition.
knowledge_statements.title: Signomial Branching Regimes

source_witnesses.locator: 2.4.2 Convergence of Multivariate Rectangular Partition Methods p. 97

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Error-Driven Branching Requires an Exhaustiveness Safeguard
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary on adaptive signomial branching based solely on current relaxation error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Selecting only a coordinate or affine argument with maximum current relaxation error does not by itself imply exhaustiveness. If an infinite descendant chain leaves some coordinate width bounded below by \(\eta>0\), then \(\operatorname{diam}(B^k)\not\to0\), boxwise envelopes need not become exact, and exhaustive-partition convergence is unavailable. Error-driven branching is convergence-safe only with an additional rule guaranteeing vanishing widths on every infinite chain, such as periodic longest-edge bisection or a tie-breaking rule with the same guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relaxation-error branching needs a width-reduction safeguard; otherwise an infinite branch may retain positive diameter.
assumptions_latex: The score may repeatedly select only a strict subset of coordinates or affine arguments.
An infinite descendant chain is possible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Error-driven selection alone does not imply exhaustiveness; every infinite branch must additionally be forced to have vanishing diameter.

notation.meaning: infinite nested chain of generated boxes
positive lower bound on an unsplit width

knowledge_statements.title: Error-Driven Branching Requires an Exhaustiveness Safeguard

children.title: Signomial Node Bounds
children.top_down_role: Regional bounds used within signomial search trees.

assumptions_latex: The original problem is a minimization problem, and each node is restricted to a log-space box \(B\).
For every retained or archived covering node \(B\), its relaxation underestimates the original objective and constraints on \(B\).
A nonempty finite collection \(\mathcal C\) of such node boxes covers the original feasible region.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
Each node value satisfies \(L_B\leq v(B)\), and \(L=
\min_{B\in\mathcal C}L_B\) is a global lower bound satisfying \(L\leq v^\star\).

notation.meaning: true optimum on node box B
node collection covering the original feasible region

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certified lower bounds attached to signomial search nodes and their aggregation over a covering collection.

source_refs.locator: 2.1.2 Partition Algorithms: A General Scheme p. 46

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a node box \(B\), let
\[L_B=\inf\{\underline F_0^B(y):\underline F_j^B(y)\leq0,\ j=1,\ldots,p,\ y\in B\},\]
where \(p\in\mathbb N\), \(y\) is the log-space decision vector, and \(\underline F_j^B\) is a valid convex underestimator of the transformed function \(F_j\) on \(B\). Then \(L_B\leq v(B)\). If a nonempty finite node collection \(\mathcal C\) covers the original feasible region, then
\[L=\min_{B\in\mathcal C}L_B\leq v^\star.\]
If a node relaxation is infeasible, the original node is infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each valid node relaxation supplies a lower bound on its box. Taking the smallest bound over node boxes covering the original feasible region gives a global lower bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Signomial Node Bounds

source_witnesses.locator: 2.1.2 Partition Algorithms: A General Scheme p. 46

children.title: Signomial Fathoming Criteria
children.top_down_role: Structural criteria for pruning signomial search regions.

assumptions_latex: A minimization node has valid lower bound \(L_B\), incumbent value \(U\), and tolerance \(\varepsilon\geq0\).
All feasibility and dominance tests used for pruning are mathematically certified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A node may be discarded only by certified infeasibility, the bound test \(L_B\geq U-\varepsilon\), or containment in a region already covered by a no-worse certified node.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe pruning tests for minimization branch-and-bound nodes.

source_refs.locator: 3.6 Finite epsilon-Convergence and epsilon-Global Optimality p. 87

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A node box \(B\) is safely fathomed if at least one of the following holds: its valid relaxation is infeasible; its lower bound satisfies \(L_B\geq U-\varepsilon\); or a valid dominance certificate shows that every feasible point in \(B\) is represented by another retained region with objective no larger. The bound test is exact when \(\varepsilon=0\). For \(\varepsilon>0\), it preserves the possibility of certifying an \(\varepsilon\)-global solution. Failure of a local nonlinear solver, absence of a locally feasible point, or a nonrigorous numerical bound is not by itself a valid fathoming criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Prune a node only when infeasibility, inability to improve the incumbent within tolerance, or valid dominance is certified; local-solver failure alone is insufficient.
knowledge_statements.title: Signomial Fathoming Criteria

source_witnesses.locator: 3.6 Finite epsilon-Convergence and epsilon-Global Optimality p. 87

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe deletion of a signomial node whose restricted original problem has been solved globally.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the original signomial problem restricted to node box \(B\) is solved globally. If it is certified infeasible, \(B\) may be fathomed. If it has optimizer \(y_B\) and value \(v(B)\), first update \(U\leftarrow\min\{U,v(B)\}\); the node may then be fathomed because its exact optimum has been incorporated into the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exactly resolved node can be deleted, but a feasible node optimizer must first update the incumbent.
assumptions_latex: The original node problem, not merely its relaxation, is solved globally.
The returned infeasibility or optimum is certified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Certified infeasibility permits immediate deletion; a finitely solved feasible node permits deletion after its optimum updates the incumbent.

notation.meaning: certified optimum of the original problem restricted to B

knowledge_statements.title: Fathoming after Exact Node Resolution

children.title: Signomial Tree Growth
children.top_down_role: Search-tree behavior under mixed-sign terms and weak relaxations.

assumptions_latex: Each processed node generates at most two children.
The root has depth \(0\), and no generated node has depth greater than \(d\), where \(d\in\mathbb Z_{\geq0}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The tree has at most \(2^d\) leaves and at most \(2^{d+1}-1\) total nodes, so its worst-case node count is exponential in \(d\).

notation.meaning: number of leaves through depth d
total generated nodes through depth d

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combinatorial worst-case size of a binary signomial partition tree.

source_refs.locator: 2.1.2 Partition Algorithms: A General Scheme p. 46

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For binary branching, level \(k\in\{0,\ldots,d\}\) contains at most \(2^k\) nodes. Therefore
\[N_{\mathrm{leaf}}(d)\leq2^d,\qquad N_{\mathrm{tot}}(d)\leq\sum_{k=0}^d2^k=2^{d+1}-1.\]
These bounds count generated relaxation subproblems. Fathoming and bound tightening can reduce the realized node count but do not change this exponential worst-case dependence on partition depth.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Binary partitioning through depth d can generate at most 2^d leaves and 2^(d+1)-1 total relaxation nodes.
knowledge_statements.title: Signomial Tree Growth

source_witnesses.locator: 2.1.2 Partition Algorithms: A General Scheme p. 46

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case depth and node count for longest-edge bisection at a prescribed log-space resolution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the root widths be \(w_i>0\), and apply longest-edge midpoint bisection. For \(\delta>0\), set \(q_i=\max\{0,\lceil\log_2(w_i/\delta)\rceil\}\) and \(D_\delta=\sum_{i=1}^n q_i\). Every descendant at depth \(D_\delta\) has each coordinate width at most \(\delta\). Thus the full unpruned tree through that resolution has at most \(2^{D_\delta}\) leaves and \(2^{D_\delta+1}-1\) nodes. If all root widths equal \(w\), the leaf bound is \(O((w/\delta)^n)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Achieving a prescribed coordinate resolution can require exponentially many bisection nodes in dimension.
assumptions_latex: The root is an \(n\)-dimensional box with finite positive widths \(w_i\).
Branching uses longest-edge midpoint bisection.
The count concerns the full unpruned binary tree.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Depth \(D_\delta=\sum_i\max\{0,\lceil\log_2(w_i/\delta)\rceil\}\) suffices, with at most \(2^{D_\delta}\) leaves and \(2^{D_\delta+1}-1\) nodes.
knowledge_statements.title: Resolution-Induced Tree-Size Bound

assumptions_latex: A node relaxation \(R_B\) contains every original feasible point in the log-space box \(B=[L,U]\).
A finite feasible incumbent value \(U^{\mathrm{inc}}\) is available for the minimization problem.
The relaxed objective \(\underline F_0^B\) underestimates the original objective \(F_0\) on \(B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Replacing each coordinate interval by its range over \(R_B^{\mathrm{cut}}\) preserves every original feasible point in \(B\) whose objective is at most \(U^{\mathrm{inc}}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimization-based coordinate tightening on a log-space node.

source_refs.locator: 1.4 Deterministic Global Optimization: Approaches and Classes of Problems p. 18

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define
\[R_B^{\mathrm{cut}}=\{y\in R_B:\underline F_0^B(y)\leq U^{\mathrm{inc}}\}.\]
For each coordinate \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\), compute
\[L_i'=\inf\{y_i:y\in R_B^{\mathrm{cut}}\},\qquad U_i'=\sup\{y_i:y\in R_B^{\mathrm{cut}}\}.\]
If \(R_B^{\mathrm{cut}}\) is empty, the node may be fathomed. Otherwise replace \([L_i,U_i]\) by \([L_i',U_i']\), using certified outward rounding when required, reconstruct the term envelopes, and repeat until the prescribed contraction tolerance is met. Every original feasible point in \(B\) with \(F_0(y)\leq U^{\mathrm{inc}}\) remains in the tightened box.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimize each log coordinate over the node relaxation with an incumbent cutoff, shrink the box to the resulting ranges, and repeat while preserving every feasible point that can match or improve the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.title: Signomial Bound Tightening

source_witnesses.locator: 1.4 Deterministic Global Optimization: Approaches and Classes of Problems p. 18

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effect of certified signomial range contraction on rebuilt boxwise relaxations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B'\subseteq B\) be obtained by certified contraction. If the model rebuilt on \(B'\) retains the restrictions of all inequalities defining the old relaxation on a common formulation space, then \(R_{B'}\subseteq R_B\cap B'\). Consequently, for minimization, \(L_{B'}\geq L_B\). Repeated certified contraction and reconstruction therefore produce nested boxes and nondecreasing valid node lower bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Feeding certified tighter ranges back into signomial envelopes strengthens the relaxation; retaining the old model ensures that lower bounds cannot decrease.
assumptions_latex: \(B'\subseteq B\) preserves every potentially improving feasible point.
The rebuilt relaxation retains the restricted previous model on a common formulation space.
Both bounds use the same minimization objective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_{B'}\subseteq R_B\cap B'\) and \(L_{B'}\geq L_B\).
knowledge_statements.title: Monotone Relaxation Feedback under Tightening

assumptions_latex: The initial log-space box \(B^0\) is compact, and every child partition exactly covers its parent.
Every infinite nested generated branch \((B_k)\) satisfies \(\operatorname{diam}(B_k)\to0\).
For every feasible limit \(\bar y\) of a nested branch, the valid node bounds are consistent: \(L_{B_k}\to F_0(\bar y)\).
Node selection is fair, and pruning uses only valid infeasibility or incumbent-bound certificates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every infinite nested branch has a unique limiting point, and the lower bounds on every feasible limiting branch converge to the objective at that point. A node containing a point improving the incumbent beyond the pruning tolerance cannot be removed by a valid bound test.

notation.meaning: valid lower bound on box B_k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spatial-refinement convergence under exhaustive rectangular branching, consistent bounds, fair selection, and safe pruning.

source_refs.locator: 2.2 Convergence Properties of Adaptive Partition Algorithms p. 59
2.4.2 Convergence of Multivariate Rectangular Partition Methods p. 97

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \((B_k)\) be an infinite nested sequence generated by the partition rule. Then
\[\operatorname{diam}(B_k)\to0,\qquad \bigcap_{k=0}^{\infty}B_k=\{\bar y\}\]
for a unique \(\bar y\in B^0\). If \(\bar y\) is feasible and the lower bounds are consistent, then
\[L_{B_k}\to F_0(\bar y).\]
Let \(U\) be the current incumbent value and let \(\varepsilon\geq0\) be the pruning tolerance. A node containing a feasible point \(y\) with \(F_0(y)<U-\varepsilon\) cannot satisfy a valid fathoming test of the form \(L_B\geq U-\varepsilon\). Under fair selection and safe pruning, exhaustive partitioning therefore localizes every indefinitely retained feasible branch while its bounds become exact at the limiting point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exhaustive rectangular branching shrinks every infinite branch to one point, and consistent node bounds become exact at each feasible branch limit. Safe pruning cannot discard a node containing an improvement larger than the tolerance.
knowledge_statements.title: Exhaustive-Partition Convergence

source_witnesses.locator: 2.2 Convergence Properties of Adaptive Partition Algorithms p. 59
2.4.2 Convergence of Multivariate Rectangular Partition Methods p. 97

assumptions_latex: The transformed feasible set is nonempty and compact, and the objective and constraints are continuous.
Branching is exhaustive, node selection is fair, and every child lower bound is no smaller than its parent lower bound.
On every shrinking nested feasible branch with limit \(\bar y\), node lower bounds converge to \(F_0(\bar y)\); shrinking branches with infeasible limits are eventually certified infeasible.
The upper-bounding procedure generates feasible trial points approaching the objective value of every feasible limiting branch that is refined indefinitely.
Incumbents are retained, and pruning uses only valid infeasibility or bound certificates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The certified global lower bounds \(L_k\) and incumbent values \(U_k\) converge to the global optimum \(v^\star\). Every accumulation point of improving incumbents is globally optimal, and termination with \(U_k-L_k\leq\varepsilon\) certifies an \(\varepsilon\)-global solution.

notation.meaning: certified global lower bound at iteration k
incumbent objective value at iteration k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global convergence of deterministic spatial branch-and-bound for transformed signomials with consistent lower- and upper-bounding operations.

source_refs.locator: 8.4 Proof of Convergence to the Global Minimum p. 282
3.6 Finite epsilon-Convergence and epsilon-Global Optimality p. 87

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At iteration \(k\), let \(L_k\) be the certified lower bound for the original feasible region obtained from the retained and archived node certificates, and let \(U_k\) be the best feasible value found. Then
\[L_k\leq v^\star\leq U_k.\]
Under exhaustive branching, fair node selection, monotone and consistent lower bounds, a consistent feasible upper-bounding procedure, and safe fathoming,
\[L_k\to v^\star\qquad\text{and}\qquad U_k\to v^\star.\]
Every accumulation point of improving feasible incumbents is globally optimal. If the algorithm terminates with \(U_k-L_k\leq\varepsilon\), where \(\varepsilon\geq0\), the returned incumbent is \(\varepsilon\)-globally optimal in absolute objective gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With exhaustive branching, fair selection, consistent lower and upper bounds, and safe pruning, certified lower bounds and feasible incumbent values converge to the global minimum. A tolerance gap certifies approximate global optimality.
knowledge_statements.title: Convergence to the Global Minimum

source_witnesses.locator: 8.4 Proof of Convergence to the Global Minimum p. 282
3.6 Finite epsilon-Convergence and epsilon-Global Optimality p. 87

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite termination of transformed-signomial spatial branch-and-bound at a fixed positive global-optimality tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\varepsilon>0\). Suppose branching has finite arity and is exhaustive, every competitive active node is processed in finite time, and there exists \(\delta>0\) such that every generated node \(B\) with \(\operatorname{diam}(B)\leq\delta\) is either certified infeasible or has a feasible trial value \(U_B\) and valid lower bound \(L_B\) satisfying \(U_B-L_B\leq\varepsilon\). With valid pruning and incumbent retention, only finitely many competitive nodes are processed before infeasibility is certified or the global gap satisfies \(U-L\leq\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform certified resolution of all sufficiently small boxes upgrades asymptotic convergence to finite termination at every fixed positive tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(\varepsilon>0\).
Branching is exhaustive and has finite arity.
Every competitive active node is processed in finite time.
For some \(\delta>0\), every generated node of diameter at most \(\delta\) is certified infeasible or has regional feasible and lower bounds differing by at most \(\varepsilon\).
Pruning is valid and incumbents are retained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm finitely certifies infeasibility or returns an incumbent satisfying \(U-L\leq\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: resolution at which every node is certifiably resolved

knowledge_statements.title: Finite Positive-Tolerance Convergence

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Positive minimum interparticle distance at a global energy minimum
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Applies to a globally minimum-potential-energy microcluster configuration.

Let q^\star=(q_1^\star,\ldots,q_N^\star) be a global minimum-potential-energy microcluster configuration and define
\[
r_{\min}(q^\star)=\min_{1\le i<j\le N}\lVert q_i^\star-q_j^\star\rVert_2.

knowledge_statements.title: Chemical-Engineering Design Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-variable chemical-design models whose complete objectives and constraints admit finite generalized-monomial representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\in\mathbb{R}_{++}^n\) denote positive design variables. Suppose every objective and constraint function defining the design problem has the form \(s_j(x)=\sum_{k=1}^{m_j}c_{jk}\prod_{i=1}^n x_i^{a_{jki}}\), where \(m_j\in\mathbb{N}\) and \(c_{jk},a_{jki}\in\mathbb{R}\). Then the design problem is a generalized signomial program. Under the componentwise substitution \(y_i=\log x_i\), each generalized monomial becomes \(c_{jk}\exp(a_{jk}^{\mathsf T}y)\), yielding an equivalent finite exponential-sum formulation. If additional physical constraints lack this form, the interface applies only to the signomial subsystem unless those constraints are reformulated equivalently.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-variable chemical-design problem is a generalized signomial program when all of its objective and constraint functions are finite signed sums of generalized monomials; logarithmic coordinates then give an equivalent exponential-sum formulation.
assumptions_latex: The design variables satisfy \(x\in\mathbb{R}_{++}^n\).
Every objective and constraint function is a finite signed sum of generalized monomials.
Any additional physical constraints are either signomial-representable or treated outside the claimed signomial classification.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The complete model is a generalized signomial program exactly under the stated representability assumption and becomes a finite exponential-sum model under \(y=\log x\).

notation.meaning: finite signed sums of generalized monomials

source_refs.locator: 9.1 Chemical Engineering Design Examples p. 289

assumptions_latex: The design parameter satisfies \(x\in\mathbb{R}_{++}^n\).
Robust stability is equivalent to finitely many inequalities \(\phi_r(x)\leq 0\).
Every \(\phi_r\) is a finite signomial.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Robust-stability design reduces to a generalized signomial program and, after \(y=\log x\), to finite exponential-sum inequalities.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite signomial encodings of robust-stability tests over positive design parameters.

source_refs.locator: 9.2 Robust Stability Analysis p. 297

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose robust stability of a parameterized system is equivalent to \(\phi_r(x)\leq 0\) for \(r=1,\ldots,R\), where \(x\in\mathbb{R}_{++}^n\) and \(\phi_r(x)=\sum_{k=1}^{m_r}c_{rk}\prod_{i=1}^n x_i^{a_{rki}}\). Then optimizing a signomial performance function subject to these tests is a generalized signomial program. With \(y_i=\log x_i\), each stability test is represented as \(\sum_k c_{rk}\exp(a_{rk}^{\mathsf T}y)\leq 0\), enabling deterministic global treatment when finite bounds and valid relaxations are supplied.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite robust-stability test expressed by signomial inequalities over positive parameters interfaces directly with generalized signomial global optimization.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded definition for the robust-stability model, preserving the source's frequency-dependent margin and its stated threshold criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A stability margin is defined by
\[
k_m(j\omega)=\inf\left\{k: P\left(j\omega,\mathbf q(k)\right)=0,\ \forall\mathbf q\in\mathcal Q\right\}.
\]
Robust stability for this model is guaranteed if and only if
\[
k_m\geq 1.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The stability margin at jω is the infimum of the values k satisfying the displayed zero condition for every q in the uncertainty set Q. For this model, robust stability is guaranteed if and only if the stability margin is at least 1.
